content.explanation: A liquid is nearly incompressible, so a hydrostatic failure releases little stored energy compared with a pneumatic test, which is far more hazardous.

content.stem: Base-metal thickness qualified by a procedure test generally establishes which of the following?
options: A qualified thickness range for production welds
The exact diameter of every production test pipe
The painted color code marked on the filler metal
The relief device set pressure for the whole vessel
content.explanation: The qualification coupon thickness sets the range of production thicknesses the WPS may be used for, per the QW-451 rules.

content.stem: Changing the welding process (for example SMAW to GTAW) on a qualified WPS requires which?
options: Only a short note added to the existing WPS document sheet
Requalification, since process is an essential variable
No action at all because both are arc welding processes
A new stamped vessel nameplate recording the process change
content.explanation: The welding process is an essential variable; switching processes requires requalification (a new PQR).

content.stem: A radiograph that is too dark to interpret most likely fails which Article 2 requirement?
options: The required penetrant dwell time on the part surface
The yoke leg spacing used during the MT examination
The allowable film-density range for the technique
The couplant applied across the inspection surface
content.explanation: Film density outside the allowable range makes the radiograph uninterpretable; density and IQI sensitivity are core Article 2 controls.

content.stem: A fluorescent penetrant examination must be viewed under which condition?
options: Bright white light in full and open daylight
Complete darkness with no light source at all
Normal shop overhead lighting without any filters
Suitable ultraviolet light in a darkened area
content.explanation: Fluorescent penetrant indications are viewed under UV-A light in a darkened area so the indications fluoresce visibly.

content.stem: The prod technique of magnetic particle testing creates the magnetic field by which means?
options: Passing current directly through the part
Spraying penetrant across the surface
Heating the part above its MDMT
Applying ultraviolet light to it
content.explanation: The prod method passes current through the part between two contacts, creating a circular field; the yoke method induces a longitudinal field instead.

content.stem: Before taking UT thickness readings, the instrument is calibrated using which of the following?
options: The vessel nameplate stamping and rating plate data
Reference blocks of known thickness and material
A penetrant developer aerosol spray can container
The relief valve set-pressure identification tag
content.explanation: Calibration on reference standards of known thickness and velocity for the material ensures accurate readings per SE-797.

content.stem: RP 572 notes that internal visual inspection is most effective when combined with which?
options: Complete removal of the vessel identification nameplate
A deliberate increase in the vessel operating pressure
Supplemental NDE such as thickness or surface methods
Painting the whole interior surface before any entry
content.explanation: Visual inspection locates suspect areas; thickness and surface NDE quantify and characterize the damage found.

content.stem: A rupture disc differs from a spring-loaded relief valve in that it does which?
options: Reseats automatically after relieving
Adjusts its set pressure during service
Measures the flow rate continuously
Bursts open and does not reclose afterward
content.explanation: A rupture disc is a non-reclosing device that bursts at its set pressure; it must be replaced after actuation, unlike a reclosing relief valve.

content.stem: Slow cooling through the critical range after welding thick carbon steel helps avoid which outcome?
options: Hard, crack-susceptible microstructure in the HAZ
A fully annealed and soft base material condition
Excess weld reinforcement on the finished weld cap
A measurable drop in the vessel rated MAWP value
content.explanation: Rapid cooling can form hard, brittle, crack-prone microstructures; preheat and controlled cooling produce tougher structures.

content.stem: Verifying filler metal against the WPS during welding inspection guards against which problem?
options: An overfilled relief valve discharge line
Use of an incorrect or unqualified consumable
A repainted and relabeled nameplate
An increased design corrosion allowance
content.explanation: Confirming the filler type/classification matches the WPS prevents wrong-consumable welds that could fail in service.

content.stem: A PMI program is especially important at which point in a project?
options: After the equipment warranty period has expired
Only during the final exterior surface paint stage
Receiving and installing alloy components
When the unit nameplate is first being stamped
content.explanation: PMI at receipt and installation catches alloy mix-ups before they enter service, which is when they are cheapest to correct.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 101 provides which of the following for the repair articles?
options: The exact set pressure for relief valves
A required paint specification for vessels
The pricing schedule for repair work
Common scope, terms, and general requirements
content.explanation: Article 101 gives the introduction and general requirements (scope, definitions, common provisions) that the specific repair articles build on.

content.stem: A butt-welded insert plate (Article 201) restores a component by doing which?
options: Welding a replacement section flush with the wall
Bolting a cover plate over the damaged wall area
Spraying a sealant compound into the thinned area
Coating the surface to build up added thickness
content.explanation: An insert plate removes the damaged area and welds in a flush replacement section, giving a permanent full-thickness repair.

content.stem: A vessel wall was 0.625 in when installed and measures 0.505 in after 16 years. Long-term rate?
options: 0.015 in/yr
0.12 in/yr
content.explanation: Long-term rate = (t_initial - t_actual)/time = (0.625 - 0.505)/16 = 0.0075 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.505 in, t_required = 0.300 in. Long-term rate 0.0075 in/yr, short-term rate 0.018 in/yr. What remaining life governs?
options: 27.3 years
11.4 years
8 years
28.1 years
content.explanation: Use the more conservative (higher) rate. Remaining life = (0.505 - 0.300)/0.018 = 11.4 years; the long-term rate would give a longer, less conservative life.

content.stem: A vessel has a remaining life of 9 years (no RBI). In how many years is the next internal or on-stream inspection due?
options: 9 years
2.2 years
4.5 years
10 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (4.5 yr) or 10 years; 4.5 years governs.

content.stem: A corroded shell: t = 0.560 in, inside radius R = 33 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 0.85. MAWP from P = SEt/(R + 0.6t)?
options: 577 psi
336 psi

content.stem: Required thickness of a spherical vessel: P = 500 psi, inside radius R = 36 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PR/(2SE - 0.2P).
content.explanation: t = (500 x 36)/((2 x 17500) - 0.2 x 500) = 0.5158 in. A sphere needs about half a cylinder's thickness for the same radius and pressure.

content.stem: A 2:1 ellipsoidal head: t = 0.500 in, inside diameter D = 60 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. MAWP from P = 2SEt/(D + 0.2t)?
content.explanation: P = (2 x 17500 x 1.0 x 0.500)/(60 + 0.2 x 0.500) = 291.2 psi. The ellipsoidal-head MAWP uses diameter D, not radius.

content.stem: A vessel has MAWP = 320 psi. The ratio of allowable stress at test temperature to design temperature is 0.95. Hydrostatic test pressure per UG-99(b)?
options: 416 psi
456 psi
304 psi
content.explanation: Test pressure = 1.3 x MAWP x (S_test/S_design) = 1.3 x 320 x 0.95 = 395.2 psi. When the ratio is below 1.0 the test pressure is reduced accordingly.

content.stem: Required thickness of a standard (6%) torispherical head: P = 250 psi, crown radius L = 60 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = 0.885PL/(SE - 0.1P).
A column has an MAWP of 90 psi at the top. A reboiler return nozzle sits 85 ft below the top (SG = 1.0). Total pressure at the nozzle?
options: 90 psi
36.8 psi
53.2 psi
content.explanation: Total = MAWP + static head = 90 + (0.433 x 85) = 126.8 psi.

content.stem: A fillet weld has a 0.75 in leg. Using the 0.7 factor, what is the effective throat?
content.explanation: Throat = 0.7 x leg = 0.7 x 0.75 = 0.525 in.

content.stem: A radial nozzle (F = 1.0) in a shell with required thickness tr = 0.350 in and finished opening d = 10 in. The available reinforcement area is 2.80 sq in. What is the reinforcement margin (available minus required area)?
options: 3.5 sq in
6.3 sq in
-0.7 sq in
7 sq in
content.explanation: Required area A = d x tr x F = 10 x 0.350 = 3.50 sq in. Margin = available - required = 2.80 - 3.50 = -0.7 sq in. A negative margin means the opening is NOT adequately reinforced.

content.stem: A vessel is being rerated to a higher MAWP. Which condition must be satisfied first?
options: The vessel has operated without incident for at least ten years
The original manufacturer has gone out of business since fabrication
The relief device is replaced with one of a smaller orifice size
Calculations confirm the higher rating with current thickness data
content.explanation: A rerating to a higher MAWP requires construction-code calculations using current thickness data, plus inspection and documentation; relief protection must suit the new rating.

content.stem: A temporary repair on an in-service vessel should be handled in which way?
options: Documented and replaced with a permanent repair as conditions allow
Treated as permanent so no further inspection is ever required again
Left undocumented because it is only a short-term field measure
Used to justify increasing the vessel rated MAWP immediately
content.explanation: Temporary repairs are documented, tracked, and made permanent (or replaced) at the next opportunity; they are not a basis for rerating.

content.stem: After repair work is complete, returning the vessel to service is authorized by whom?
options: The welding crew once they finish depositing the final pass
The authorized inspector after acceptance of the completed work
The operations supervisor regardless of inspection status
The coating contractor after the exterior is fully painted
content.explanation: The authorized inspector authorizes return to service once the repair and its required NDE/testing are accepted.

content.stem: The extent of NDE applied to a repair weld should be based on which consideration?
options: Whichever single method happens to be quickest for the crew on shift
The exterior paint color and finish scheme chosen for that vessel
The repair method, service severity, and applicable code requirements
The number of operators that happen to be available that day
content.explanation: NDE extent follows the repair type, service severity, and the construction/inspection code requirements, not convenience.

content.stem: On-stream inspection of a pressure vessel is best described as inspection performed while it is:
options: Shut down, opened, drained, and fully entered for access
Disconnected and removed entirely from its foundation
Pressurized only to the full hydrostatic test pressure
Operating, using external or non-intrusive techniques
content.explanation: On-stream inspection is done with the vessel operating, using external thickness/surface methods; internal inspection requires shutdown and entry.

content.stem: The frequency of thickness measurements at a CML should be governed primarily by which factor?
options: The corrosion rate and the remaining life of the component
The exterior paint condition observed at the last inspection
The total headcount of inspectors assigned to the unit
The font size used on the vessel identification nameplate
content.explanation: Thickness monitoring frequency is driven by corrosion rate and remaining life so wall loss is caught before it threatens integrity.

content.stem: Which document set should be available to support a vessel's integrity decisions?
options: Only the single most recent external inspection checklist on file
Design data, inspection history, and repair and alteration records
Just the purchase order and the original equipment delivery invoice
Only the coating manufacturer data sheet for the applied topcoat
content.explanation: Integrity decisions rely on the full permanent record: design/construction data, inspection history, and repair/alteration records.

content.stem: Where a jurisdiction has adopted API 510, its role with respect to the code is generally to:
options: Perform every thickness reading on the owner's behalf
Write the welding procedures used by the repair team
Enforce the applicable legal requirements within its area
Approve the exterior paint scheme for each vessel
content.explanation: The jurisdiction enforces the legal/regulatory requirements; the owner/user runs the program and the inspector accepts the work.

content.stem: Condensate corrosion in steam systems is commonly reduced by which of the following measures?
options: Raising the dissolved oxygen content of the boiler feedwater
Lowering the overall system pH well down into the acidic range
Removing all inspection of the condensate piping runs entirely
Removing dissolved gases and correcting the water chemistry
content.explanation: Deaeration and proper chemical treatment (pH/oxygen control) limit condensate corrosion from dissolved O2 and carbonic acid.

content.stem: Caustic corrosion (gouging) of carbon steel is most likely to localize at which areas?
options: High-heat-flux or deposit locations where caustic concentrates
Cold, well-mixed regions that have no heat input at all present
Externally insulated and fully dry shell sections of the vessel
Inert-gas blanketed vapor spaces located above the liquid level
content.explanation: Caustic concentrates under deposits and at high heat flux, producing localized gouging at those spots.

content.stem: High-temperature H2/H2S corrosion rates in hydroprocessing are commonly estimated using which?
options: The API 941 Nelson curves used for HTHA screening only
The modified Couper-Gorman curves for the alloy and conditions
The Larson-Miller parameter applied to creep rupture data
The Goodman diagram describing the fatigue endurance limit
content.explanation: The modified Couper-Gorman curves give H2/H2S corrosion rates by alloy, temperature, and H2S content; Nelson curves are for HTHA, a different mechanism.

content.stem: An austenitic stainless component cracked in service; which finding best supports chloride SCC?
options: Uniform general wall thinning with no cracking present anywhere at all
A single straight crack located in a fully compressive stress field
Branched transgranular cracks with chlorides and tensile stress present
Surface rusting that is typical of plain carbon steel in wet humid air
content.explanation: Cl-SCC characteristically shows branched (often transgranular) cracking in austenitic stainless under chlorides, tensile stress, and temperature.

content.stem: Which wet H2S damage form involves stacked, through-wall-linked cracks driven by hydrogen and stress?
options: Simple uniform atmospheric rusting of the surface
High-temperature sulfidation of the bare metal
Chloride stress corrosion cracking of stainless
Stress-oriented hydrogen-induced cracking (SOHIC)
content.explanation: SOHIC is stacked HIC-type cracking aligned by tensile stress, often near welds; it requires hydrogen charging plus stress.

content.stem: Which design or maintenance practice most reduces atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel?
options: Maintaining a sound protective coating and good drainage
Allowing water to pool against the steel for long periods
Removing all coatings so the surface can breathe freely
Adding chloride salts to the surrounding environment
content.explanation: Sound coatings, good drainage, and avoiding standing water and salts are the primary controls for atmospheric corrosion.

content.stem: ASME VIII-1 (UG-22) requires that vessel design consider which of the following?
options: Only the internal design pressure acting by itself alone
All applicable loadings such as pressure, weight, and wind
Just the exterior paint weight added to the shell mass
Solely the relief valve set pressure during an upset
content.explanation: UG-22 requires considering all applicable loads - internal/external pressure, dead/live weight, wind, seismic, thermal, and nozzle loads, as relevant.

content.stem: For vessels in lethal service, ASME VIII-1 imposes which additional requirement?
options: A reduction in the required minimum wall thickness used
Permission to skip the post-weld heat treatment entirely
Full radiography and butt joints with stricter weld controls
An exemption from any form of pressure or leak testing
content.explanation: Lethal-service vessels require full RT of main joints, specific joint types, and (typically) PWHT for carbon/low-alloy steels - stricter, not relaxed.

content.stem: The extent of radiography required by UW-11 for a given vessel depends chiefly on which factors?
options: The exterior color and the surface finish chosen for the vessel shell
The number of nozzles installed on the bottom head of the vessel only
The brand of welding machine used by the fabrication shop on the job
The joint efficiency used, the service, and the material thickness
content.explanation: RT extent under UW-11 follows the joint efficiency taken in design, the service (e.g., lethal), and material/thickness rules.

content.stem: Under UCS-66, assigning a steel to toughness curve A rather than curve D means it generally:
options: Requires a warmer MDMT before impact testing is exempted
Is exempt from impact testing at all possible temperatures
Has no relationship between thickness and exemption limits
Is automatically acceptable for any cryogenic service use
content.explanation: Curve A materials have the least favorable toughness, so they need a warmer MDMT (or impact testing) compared with curve D materials at the same thickness.

content.stem: A welder's performance qualification is generally considered to remain in effect as long as:
options: The welder stays employed by the very same contractor company only
The welder uses the process within a set period without a long break
The original welder test coupon is physically retained on file still
The vessel nameplate continues to list that welder by name and number
content.explanation: A welder's qualification stays valid while the process is used within the allowed interval (e.g., six months) without an extended lapse.

content.stem: Qualifying a procedure on one base metal can cover other metals in the same group because:
options: Grouped metals always share the identical chemical formula
Grouping is based purely on the cost of the base metal
Grouped metals share similar weldability characteristics
Grouping reflects only the color marking on the metal
content.explanation: P-Number grouping reflects similar weldability, so qualification on one member can cover others, reducing the number of tests required.

content.stem: Geometric unsharpness in radiography is reduced by doing which of the following?
options: Increasing the film density well beyond the allowed range
Removing the image quality indicator from the setup
Using a much larger effective focal-spot source size
Increasing source-to-film distance and minimizing the gap
content.explanation: Geometric unsharpness drops with longer source-to-film distance, a smaller focal spot, and the object close to the film.

content.stem: Penetrant examination is generally limited by a temperature range because outside it:
options: Penetrant behavior and sensitivity can change significantly
The part will instantly crack from the thermal shock applied
The developer becomes permanently bonded to the surface
The vessel MAWP rating is automatically reduced by half
content.explanation: Penetrant viscosity and sensitivity depend on temperature; standard procedures specify a range (with qualification needed outside it).

content.stem: Demagnetization after magnetic particle testing may be necessary to prevent which problem?
options: The part becoming permanently radioactive after the test
Residual magnetism interfering with later machining or service
The penetrant developer from drying on the surface too soon
The vessel from exceeding its rated MAWP during operation
content.explanation: Residual magnetism can attract debris or disturb instruments/welding later, so demagnetization is performed when needed.

content.stem: When direct visual access to an internal area is limited, RP 572 suggests using which aid?
options: A heavier coat of exterior paint over the suspect area
An increase in the operating pressure during the check
Remote visual tools such as borescopes or cameras
Removal of the vessel nameplate to improve the view
content.explanation: Borescopes, video probes, and similar remote visual tools extend inspection into areas with limited direct access.

content.stem: A pilot-operated relief valve is sometimes selected over a conventional spring valve because it:
options: Eliminates the need for any periodic inspection at all
Raises the protected vessel's rated MAWP automatically
Measures the process flow rate continuously in service
Can operate closer to set pressure with stable seating
content.explanation: Pilot-operated valves can operate nearer set pressure with good seat tightness, useful where the margin between operating and set pressure is small.

content.stem: Carbon equivalent (CE) of a steel is used during welding planning mainly to gauge which?
options: The hardenability and the need for preheat or controls
The exact purchase price of the base material plate
The color code to be painted on the finished weld
The set pressure required for the relief device used
content.explanation: A higher carbon equivalent indicates greater hardenability and cracking risk, signaling the need for preheat and hydrogen control.

content.stem: Undercut at the toe of a weld is a concern primarily because it:
options: Adds beneficial reinforcement to the completed weld cap
Creates a stress concentration that can initiate cracking
Improves the fatigue life of the welded connection
Lowers the carbon content of the deposited weld metal
content.explanation: Undercut is a sharp groove at the weld toe that concentrates stress and can nucleate fatigue or brittle cracks; limits apply in the code.

content.stem: A PMI finding that a component is the wrong alloy should lead to which action?
options: Immediate acceptance since the part physically fits
Repainting the component to match the surrounding parts
Evaluation and correction before the item enters service
Raising the corrosion allowance to cover the difference
content.explanation: A confirmed material mix-up is evaluated and corrected (replace or re-rate) before service, since the wrong alloy can fail prematurely.

content.stem: When weld overlay (Article 211) is used for corrosion resistance, a key control is to:
options: Maximize base-metal dilution into the overlay deposit
Skip any examination of the finished overlay surface
Apply the overlay only after the vessel is retired
Achieve the required dilution and chemistry at the surface
content.explanation: Corrosion-resistant overlay must reach the specified surface chemistry, which means controlling dilution; the overlay is then examined.

content.stem: In flaw excavation and weld repair (Article 304), confirming complete flaw removal is done by:
options: Examining the cavity with PT or MT before re-welding
Assuming removal once the grinder reaches any depth
Painting the cavity and returning it to service
Measuring the exterior paint thickness over the area
content.explanation: After excavation the cavity is examined (PT or MT) to confirm the flaw is fully removed before and during weld repair.

content.stem: A CML read 0.610 in 12 years ago and reads 0.430 in today. What is the long-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.015 in/yr
0.03 in/yr
content.explanation: Rate = (t_initial - t_actual)/time = (0.610 - 0.430)/12 = 0.015 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.430 in, t_required = 0.225 in, corrosion rate = 0.015 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 28.7 years
13.7 years
6.8 years
15 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.430 - 0.225)/0.015 = 13.7 years.

content.stem: A vessel's remaining life is 24 years with no RBI assessment. Maximum internal inspection interval?
options: 12 years
24 years
10 years
6 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (12 yr) or 10 years; the 10-year cap governs at 10 years.

content.stem: A corroded shell: t = 0.375 in, inside radius R = 24 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. MAWP from P = SEt/(R + 0.6t)?
Required thickness of a hemispherical head: P = 450 psi, inside radius R = 24 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PR/(2SE - 0.2P).
content.explanation: t = (450 x 24)/((2 x 17500) - 0.2 x 450) = 0.3094 in. Using the cylinder formula (about double) or the diameter in place of radius are the common errors.

content.stem: Required thickness of a 2:1 ellipsoidal head: P = 300 psi, inside diameter D = 72 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PD/(2SE - 0.2P).
content.explanation: t = (300 x 72)/((2 x 17500) - 0.2 x 300) = 0.6182 in. Using radius instead of diameter, or the cylinder formula, are the common errors.

content.stem: A vessel has MAWP = 360 psi and equal allowable stresses at test and design temperature. Standard hydrostatic test pressure per UG-99(b)?
options: 540 psi
360 psi
468 psi
396 psi
content.explanation: Test pressure = 1.3 x MAWP x (S_test/S_design) = 1.3 x 360 x 1.0 = 468 psi. The 1.5x factor is the older pre-1999 basis.

content.stem: A pneumatic test per UG-100 uses a multiplier of 1.1 times MAWP (stress ratio = 1.0). For a vessel with MAWP = 300 psi, what is the pneumatic test pressure?
options: 390 psi
450 psi
300 psi
330 psi
content.explanation: Pneumatic test pressure = 1.1 x MAWP x (S_test/S_design) = 1.1 x 300 = 330 psi. The 1.1x factor is the current ASME VIII-1 UG-100 value (confirmed for the 2023/2025 editions) and is lower than the 1.3x hydrostatic factor because compressed gas stores far more energy. Confirm the multiplier against your effectivity edition, as test factors have changed across editions.

content.stem: A vertical vessel has an MAWP of 120 psi at the top. A bottom drain nozzle is 60 ft below the top (SG = 1.0). Total pressure at the drain nozzle?
options: 146 psi
120 psi
26 psi
94 psi
content.explanation: Total = MAWP + static head = 120 + (0.433 x 60) = 146 psi.

content.stem: A fillet weld requires a 0.42 in throat. Using the 0.7 factor, what leg dimension is needed?
options: 0.6 in

content.stem: A single-welded butt joint made WITHOUT a backing strip (Type 3) can be assigned what maximum joint efficiency per Table UW-12?
content.explanation: A Type 3 joint (single butt, no backing) is limited to E = 0.60 in Table UW-12 and cannot be radiographed for higher credit.

content.stem: Localized, sharp-edged grooving is found in a high-velocity line carrying high-TAN crude at about 600 F. Which damage mechanism best fits?
options: High-temperature hydrogen attack
Caustic stress corrosion cracking
Atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel
Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC)
content.explanation: High velocity, high total acid number (TAN), and elevated temperature producing localized grooving is the signature of naphthenic acid corrosion.

content.stem: A Cr-Mo reactor in high-pressure hydrogen service shows internal decarburization and grain-boundary fissuring. Which mechanism is indicated?
options: High-temperature hydrogen attack
Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC)
Chloride stress corrosion cracking
Caustic corrosion (gouging)
content.explanation: Internal decarburization and methane-driven fissuring at grain boundaries under high H2 partial pressure and temperature is HTHA, screened with the API 941 Nelson curves.

content.stem: An austenitic stainless line develops branched, transgranular cracks where chlorides concentrate and tensile stress is present. Which mechanism fits?
options: Sulfidation (sulfidic corrosion)
Chloride stress corrosion cracking
Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC)
Caustic corrosion (gouging)
content.explanation: Branched, usually transgranular cracking of austenitic stainless under chlorides, tensile stress, and temperature is classic chloride SCC.

content.stem: Wet, damaged insulation with rust staining is found on a carbon-steel vessel operating around 200 F. Which mechanism is the prime suspect?
options: Sulfidation (sulfidic corrosion)
Chloride stress corrosion cracking
Corrosion under insulation (CUI)
High-temperature hydrogen attack
content.explanation: Trapped moisture under insulation against carbon steel in the susceptible temperature band points to CUI.

content.stem: Localized gouging is found beneath deposits in a high-heat-flux zone where sodium hydroxide can concentrate. Which mechanism fits?
options: Atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel
Chloride stress corrosion cracking
Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC)
Caustic corrosion (gouging)
content.explanation: Caustic concentrating under deposits at high heat flux produces localized gouging - caustic corrosion.

content.stem: Cracking is found at non-PWHT carbon-steel welds in a unit handling alkanolamine solution. Which mechanism is most likely?
options: Amine stress corrosion cracking
Atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel
Sulfidation (sulfidic corrosion)
Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC)
content.explanation: Cracking at highly stressed (non-PWHT) carbon-steel welds in amine service is amine SCC; PWHT is the principal mitigation.

content.stem: General wall thinning is observed on carbon steel operating near 600 F in a sulfur-bearing stream. Which mechanism fits?
options: Chloride stress corrosion cracking
Sulfidation (sulfidic corrosion)
Corrosion under insulation (CUI)
Caustic corrosion (gouging)
content.explanation: Carbon steel above roughly 450-500 F in sulfur-bearing streams thins by sulfidation; rate rises with temperature, sulfur, and low silicon.

content.stem: A vessel fractures with little deformation at low metal temperature, initiating from a flaw under tensile stress. Which mechanism is indicated?
options: Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC)
Caustic corrosion (gouging)
Brittle fracture at low temperature
Sulfidation (sulfidic corrosion)
content.explanation: Low temperature, a flaw, and tensile stress in a low-toughness material producing a fast fracture with little ductility is brittle fracture.

content.stem: An effective inspection plan for a vessel should be built primarily around which of the following?
options: The exterior paint scheme and the chosen jacket color
The number of inspectors available on a given shift
The brand of ultrasonic instrument owned by the shop
The credible damage mechanisms and their likely locations
content.explanation: Inspection planning targets the credible damage mechanisms and where they occur, selecting methods and CMLs accordingly.

content.stem: A vessel subject to frequent pressure or thermal cycling should have its inspection plan address:
options: Fatigue cracking at stress-concentration details
Only uniform general thinning of the shell course
Just the exterior coating condition over time
Solely the legibility of the vessel nameplate
content.explanation: Cyclic service raises fatigue risk at nozzles, attachments, and other stress concentrators, which the plan should target with surface NDE.

content.stem: When hydrotesting a vessel, controlling the metal temperature to a suitable minimum guards against:
options: An automatic increase of the vessel MAWP
Brittle fracture during the pressurized test
The need to document the test in records
The relief valve opening at its set point
content.explanation: Hydrotest at too low a metal temperature risks brittle fracture; a minimum temperature (often tied to MDMT) is maintained during the test.

content.stem: An alteration that affects the pressure-containing capability of a vessel requires which of these?
options: Only a verbal sign-off from the operations shift supervisor
Nothing more than a routine external visual inspection pass
Engineering design review per the applicable construction code
A simple repaint of the altered area once the work is done
content.explanation: Alterations are designed and reviewed per the construction code, then inspected, tested, and documented - more involved than a routine repair.

content.stem: When new thickness data show the corrosion rate is higher than previously assumed, the inspector should:
options: Ignore the new readings until the next scheduled unit outage
Increase the vessel MAWP rating to offset the added metal loss
Repaint the exterior surface to slow the internal corrosion
Recalculate remaining life and adjust the inspection interval
content.explanation: A higher measured rate shortens remaining life, so the remaining life and inspection interval are recalculated and tightened as needed.

content.stem: As part of vessel integrity, the inspector should confirm the pressure-relief device is:
options: Correctly set, in service, and not isolated or blocked
Painted to match the surrounding vessel surfaces
Removed entirely to simplify the inspection work
Set above the vessel MAWP to avoid nuisance lifts
content.explanation: Overpressure protection depends on the relief device being correctly set, in service, and with its inlet/outlet not blocked or improperly isolated.

content.stem: For a thin cylindrical shell under internal pressure, which joint usually governs the required thickness?
options: The circumferential joint, which carries the larger stress
The longitudinal joint, which carries the larger hoop stress
Neither joint, since both carry identical stresses always
The nozzle attachment weld, regardless of the shell stress
content.explanation: Hoop stress (resisted by the longitudinal joint) is about twice the axial stress, so the longitudinal joint generally governs shell thickness.

content.stem: The nameplate (UG-116) of an ASME VIII-1 vessel provides which of the following?
options: Only the exterior paint color and finish specification
Just the name of the welder who built the vessel
The Code stamp, MAWP, temperatures, and manufacturer data
Only the date the last inspection was performed
content.explanation: The UG-116 nameplate carries the Code mark, MAWP, design temperatures, MDMT, manufacturer, and serial/national-board data.

content.stem: A proof test under UG-101 may be used when which situation applies?
options: The manufacturer would simply prefer to skip the hydrotest
The vessel needs its rated MAWP raised without any real basis
The relief device cannot be located anywhere on the vessel
The strength of a part cannot be computed with confidence
content.explanation: UG-101 proof testing establishes MAWP for parts whose strength cannot be calculated reliably, by test rather than by formula.

content.stem: UW-13 governs the attachment details for which vessel feature?
options: Heads and the transition to the adjoining shell
Only the exterior coating over the weld seams
Just the nameplate bracket on the shell wall
Solely the relief device discharge piping run
content.explanation: UW-13 covers head-to-shell and similar attachment-weld details, including acceptable joint geometries and weld sizes.

content.stem: UCS-57 establishes radiography requirements that depend chiefly on which factor?
options: The exterior paint thickness applied to the shell
The material and the joint thickness above set limits
The number of operators present during welding
The brand of consumables used for the weld
content.explanation: UCS-57 requires RT of certain carbon/low-alloy steel joints once thickness exceeds tabulated limits, tied to the material.

content.stem: Qualifying a welder in the vertical and overhead positions on plate generally covers which?
options: Only the exact coupon orientation that was welded
Every pipe diameter without any further testing
Those positions plus the flat and horizontal on plate
Only fillet welds and never any groove welds
content.explanation: Position qualification follows QW-461 rules; qualifying in the harder positions typically also covers the easier ones within the applicable scope.

content.stem: Guided-bend tests in a procedure qualification are used chiefly to evaluate which property?
options: The exact cost of the filler metal consumed
The color code marked on the base material
The relief device set pressure for the vessel
Soundness and ductility of the weld and the HAZ
content.explanation: Guided-bend tests reveal weld/HAZ soundness and ductility by bending the specimen and inspecting for opened discontinuities.

content.stem: A radiographic technique using a wire-type IQI demonstrates adequate sensitivity by which means?
options: The required wire diameter being visible on the film
The film simply being dark across the whole image
The penetrant developer drying within the dwell time
The couplant being applied across the test surface
content.explanation: Wire IQI sensitivity is shown when the specified essential wire is visible on the radiograph, confirming the technique reveals small discontinuities.

content.stem: When a UT thickness reading appears abnormally thin, a prudent first step is to:
options: Immediately condemn the entire vessel without any rechecking
Recheck calibration and surface condition before accepting it
Raise the operating pressure to try to confirm the reading
Repaint the surface and then take no further readings at all
content.explanation: Abnormal readings are verified by rechecking calibration, couplant, and surface condition (scale, pitting) before being accepted as real wall loss.

content.stem: During external inspection, RP 572 directs attention to supports and saddles mainly because they:
options: Always carry the vessel identification nameplate
Are never in contact with the vessel shell wall
Can trap moisture and corrode at contact points
Set the required hydrostatic test pressure value
content.explanation: Support/saddle contact areas trap moisture and debris, creating crevice/contact corrosion that is easy to miss.

content.stem: A block valve installed between a vessel and its relief device must be managed so that it:
options: Stays closed to protect the relief valve from fouling
Replaces the need to inspect the relief device itself
Sets the relief device opening pressure during service
Is car-sealed or locked open to keep relief available
content.explanation: Isolation valves on relief paths are administratively controlled (car-sealed/locked open) so the relief path is never inadvertently blocked.

content.stem: Welding inspection activities are best organized into which sequence?
options: Before, during, and after welding checks
Only a single check after all welding is done
Only a check before the first arc is struck
Only a review of the final exterior paint coat
content.explanation: RP 577 frames inspection as before (materials, fit-up, WPS), during (parameters, interpass), and after (NDE, acceptance) welding.

content.stem: Records of a PMI program should capture which of the following for traceability?
options: Only the assigned painter and the applied topcoat batch number
The component, the method, and the verified alloy result
Just the operator rest and meal break times during the testing
Only the relief device set pressure recorded at the time
content.explanation: PMI records document what was tested, the method used, and the confirmed material, supporting traceability and audits.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 215 gives repair-welding considerations specifically for which material family?
options: Aboveground storage tank carbon-steel bottoms
Copper-alloy condenser and exchanger tubing
Cr-Mo (chromium-molybdenum) steel pressure vessels
Austenitic stainless atmospheric tank roofs
content.explanation: Article 215 addresses repair welding of Cr-Mo steel pressure vessels (preheat, temper bead, PWHT concerns). It is in 510's PCC-2 scope, not 570's.

content.stem: In-service welding (Article 210) procedures must specifically control which two risks?
options: Excess cleanliness and over-application of coating
Nameplate damage and loss of the serial number
Reduced flow rate and increased pumping power use
Burn-through and hydrogen (heat-affected-zone) cracking
content.explanation: Welding on pressurized, flowing equipment risks burn-through (thin hot wall) and hydrogen cracking from fast cooling; the procedure controls both.

content.stem: A CML read 0.580 in eight years ago and reads 0.420 in today. Long-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.02 in/yr
0.04 in/yr
0.01 in/yr
content.explanation: Rate = (t_initial - t_actual)/time = (0.580 - 0.420)/8 = 0.02 in/yr.

content.stem: A vessel was built with a 0.125 in corrosion allowance and corrodes at 0.010 in/yr. After how many years is the corrosion allowance fully consumed?
options: 0 years
12.5 years
6.2 years
0.1 years
content.explanation: Years to consume CA = corrosion allowance / rate = 0.125/0.010 = 12.5 years.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.420 in, t_required = 0.260 in, corrosion rate = 0.020 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 21 years
4 years
8 years
13 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.420 - 0.260)/0.020 = 8 years.

content.stem: A vessel's remaining life is 14 years with no RBI assessment. Maximum internal inspection interval?
options: 14 years
3.5 years
10 years
7 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (7 yr) or 10 years; 7 years governs.

content.stem: A vessel's shell MAWP computes to 312 psi and its head MAWP to 348 psi at the same conditions. Which value is the vessel MAWP?
options: 312 psi
348 psi
330 psi
660 psi
content.explanation: The vessel MAWP is set by the limiting (lowest) component, so the shell governs at 312 psi.

content.stem: Required shell thickness (circumferential stress): P = 375 psi, R = 42 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PR/(SE - 0.6P).
Required thickness of a 2:1 ellipsoidal head: P = 260 psi, inside diameter D = 90 in, S = 17500 psi, E = 1.0. Use t = PD/(2SE - 0.2P).
content.explanation: t = (260 x 90)/((2 x 17500) - 0.2 x 260) = 0.6696 in. Using radius instead of diameter, or the cylinder formula, are the common errors.

content.stem: A hemispherical head: t = 0.420 in, inside radius R = 42 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0. MAWP from P = 2SEt/(R + 0.2t)?
A vessel has MAWP = 275 psi and a test-to-design stress ratio of 1.10. Hydrostatic test pressure per UG-99(b)?
content.explanation: Test pressure = 1.3 x MAWP x (S_test/S_design) = 1.3 x 275 x 1.10 = 393.3 psi.

content.stem: A column has an MAWP of 110 psi at the top. A feed nozzle sits 45 ft below the top (SG = 1.0). Total pressure at the feed nozzle?
options: 110 psi
19.5 psi
90.5 psi
content.explanation: Total = MAWP + static head = 110 + (0.433 x 45) = 129.5 psi.

content.stem: A fillet weld has a 0.875 in leg. Using the 0.7 factor, what is the effective throat?
Per UG-16(b), the minimum thickness of shells and heads (after forming, excluding corrosion allowance) for most ASME VIII-1 vessels is generally:
content.explanation: UG-16(b) sets a general minimum thickness of 1/16 in (1.5 mm), exclusive of corrosion allowance, for shells and heads (with specific exceptions for certain services such as compressed air and steam).

content.stem: A hydroprocessing reactor circuit shows accelerated corrosion where hydrogen and hydrogen sulfide coexist at high temperature. Which mechanism is indicated?
options: High-temperature H2/H2S corrosion
Brittle fracture at low temperature
Atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel
Caustic stress corrosion cracking
content.explanation: Accelerated metal loss where H2 and H2S coexist at high temperature is high-temperature H2/H2S corrosion, estimated with the modified Couper-Gorman curves.

content.stem: A carbon-steel vessel in wet H2S service develops mid-wall, planar cracks at inclusions without any applied stress. Which mechanism best fits?
options: Chloride stress corrosion cracking
Hydrogen-induced cracking (HIC)
Naphthenic acid corrosion (NAC)
Caustic corrosion (gouging)
content.explanation: Planar cracks at mid-wall inclusions driven by hydrogen, occurring without applied stress, are HIC; SSC and SOHIC instead require tensile stress.

content.stem: A carbon-steel line shows uniform thinning and rust where it is exposed to humid marine air with wet/dry cycling. Which mechanism fits?
options: High-temperature H2/H2S corrosion
Chloride stress corrosion cracking
Atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel
Caustic corrosion (gouging)
content.explanation: Uniform thinning and rust in humid, chloride-laden marine air with wet/dry cycling is atmospheric corrosion of carbon steel.

content.stem: A vessel that can experience full vacuum during operation or steam-out must be evaluated for:
options: Only the internal design pressure acting outward alone
Just the exterior coating condition over its service life
Solely the legibility of the installed vessel nameplate
External pressure (buckling) in addition to internal pressure
content.explanation: Vacuum or external pressure conditions require an external-pressure (buckling) check per UG-28, not only the internal-pressure design.

content.stem: Weld overlay is sometimes applied during a repair primarily to accomplish which of the following?
options: Restore wall thickness or add a corrosion-resistant layer
Increase the overall outside diameter of the component
Lower the rated MAWP of the repaired vessel section
Replace the requirement for any post-repair inspection
content.explanation: Weld overlay/buildup restores lost wall or provides a corrosion-resistant surface; the deposit is then examined per the procedure.

content.stem: A fillet-welded patch over a corroded area is acceptable only when which condition is satisfied?
options: It is installed without any engineering evaluation at all
It is evaluated for the service, stresses, and remaining wall
It permanently raises the rated MAWP of the vessel shell
It eliminates the need to track or re-inspect that area
content.explanation: Lap/fillet-welded patches require evaluation of service, stress, and remaining wall, and are typically tracked as temporary until made permanent.

content.stem: When checking a cylindrical shell for external pressure, the controlling failure mode is usually:
options: Tensile rupture of the longitudinal weld seam
Brittle fracture of the bottom head only
Elastic or inelastic buckling of the shell
Fatigue cracking at the nameplate bracket
content.explanation: External pressure design (UG-28) guards against buckling/collapse, evaluated with the Factor A/B charts, rather than tensile rupture.

content.stem: Dead legs and infrequently used connections deserve attention in an inspection plan because they:
options: Always carry the highest flow and the least corrosion present
Are exempt from the vessel inspection program requirements
Only matter for the exterior coating and never the metal
Can corrode unseen where stagnant fluid or condensate collects
content.explanation: Stagnant dead legs accumulate water/condensate and corrode unseen, so they are deliberately included in inspection planning.

content.stem: The MAWP marked on a vessel's nameplate represents which of the following?
options: The maximum gauge pressure permitted at the top in the operating position
The pressure used only during the hydrostatic test of the vessel shell
The minimum pressure the vessel must always be kept safely above
The exterior atmospheric pressure surrounding the vessel shell wall
content.explanation: MAWP is the maximum gauge pressure permitted at the top of the vessel in its operating position, accounting for static head and the limiting component.

content.stem: When a repair on a thick carbon-steel vessel would normally require PWHT, omitting it requires:
options: Only the informal verbal agreement of the operations shift crew
A code-recognized alternative such as controlled-deposition welding
Nothing at all, since PWHT is always optional for any repair
An automatic reduction of the vessel rated MAWP value applied
content.explanation: Where PWHT is impractical, a code-recognized alternative (e.g., temper-bead/controlled-deposition per PCC-2 209) must be used and qualified.

content.stem: The UG-16(b) minimum-thickness rule for shells and heads is stated to be applied:
options: Including the full corrosion allowance in the value
Only after the vessel has entered active service
Exclusive of any corrosion allowance that is added
Solely to the exterior painted surface of the wall
content.explanation: The UG-16(b) minimum thickness (generally 1/16 in) is exclusive of corrosion allowance; the CA is added on top of the pressure and minimum requirements.

content.stem: UG-25 requires that vessels subject to corrosion be provided with which of the following?
options: An automatic increase of the design pressure over time
A thinner wall to encourage uniform general corrosion
A coating in place of any wall-thickness considerations
A suitable corrosion allowance or other protective provision
content.explanation: UG-25 requires accounting for corrosion/erosion by adding a corrosion allowance or other means so the vessel meets its design life.

content.stem: UG-36 allows certain small openings to be exempt from reinforcement calculations based on:
options: Their finished diameter and spacing being within set limits
The exterior paint color applied in the area around the opening
The number of welding operators present during the work shift
The brand of cutting drill used to make the finished opening
content.explanation: Small openings within UG-36 size and spacing limits need no reinforcement calculation, provided the other conditions are met.

content.stem: UCS-79 limits the extreme fiber elongation from cold forming because excessive cold work can:
options: Increase the vessel rated MAWP without any check
Reduce material toughness and require heat treatment
Improve corrosion resistance in every environment
Eliminate the need for any post-forming inspection
content.explanation: Excessive cold-forming strain reduces ductility/toughness, so UCS-79 limits it and may require heat treatment above defined strain levels.

content.stem: Standard flanges selected from a recognized dimensional standard (UG-44) are acceptable when:
options: They are painted to match the surrounding vessel shell surface
The operator prefers them over calculated custom flange designs
Their pressure-temperature rating covers the design conditions
They are installed without any gasket between the flange faces
content.explanation: Standard flanges are acceptable when their pressure-temperature rating (e.g., ASME B16.5) covers the design pressure and temperature.

content.stem: Removing weld backing where it was used in qualification is treated in Section IX as:
options: An administrative item with no bearing on the finished weld
A valid reason to raise the vessel's rated MAWP pressure value
A change only to the exterior surface paint specification used
A change that may require attention as a defined variable
content.explanation: Backing (its presence/removal) is addressed among Section IX welding variables; changes are evaluated against the essential/nonessential rules for the process.

content.stem: When impact (toughness) testing is required for a weld, Section IX treats the relevant items as:
options: Supplementary essential variables for the qualification
Purely administrative variables with no testing needed
A substitute for the vessel hydrostatic pressure test
A reason to skip the base-metal P-Number grouping
content.explanation: When notch-toughness is required, certain variables become supplementary essential variables, adding to the essential variables that must be controlled.

content.stem: Section V, Article 1 assigns responsibility for verifying NDE personnel qualification to:
options: The painter who applies the final exterior protective topcoat
The organization performing the examination (the Owner/User's agent)
The operations crew running the process unit during that shift
The jurisdiction that has adopted the relevant construction code
content.explanation: Article 1 places responsibility for qualified procedures and personnel on the organization performing the NDE, per the referencing code section.

content.stem: Coating or scale left on a surface during UT thickness measurement can cause readings that are:
options: Always exactly correct regardless of the surface condition present
Lower than actual by removing the back-wall coating echo signal
Erroneous, often reading high by including the coating
Completely independent of the surface coating condition entirely
content.explanation: Coatings/scale can be measured as part of the wall, giving a falsely high reading; surface prep or coating compensation is needed.

content.stem: RP 572 recommends inspecting ladder, platform, and davit attachments to a vessel because they:
options: They carry the vessel nameplate and the serial number plate data
They set the required hydrostatic test pressure value for testing
They are never welded onto the pressure-boundary shell wall
Introduce local stresses and crevices where cracking can start
content.explanation: Welded external attachments create local stress risers and crevices, which warrant surface NDE at the attachment welds.

content.stem: RP 576 notes that an undersized or fouled relief device discharge line can:
options: Cause backpressure that impairs the device's capacity
Increase the protected vessel's rated MAWP value
Eliminate the need to inspect the relief device
Improve the device's seat tightness in service
content.explanation: Restricted or undersized discharge piping raises backpressure, which can reduce relieving capacity or cause valve instability.

content.stem: Confirming joint fit-up and root opening before welding helps the inspector prevent which defect?
options: An overfilled relief valve discharge line
Incomplete penetration at the weld root
A repainted and relabeled vessel nameplate
An increased design corrosion allowance value
content.explanation: Correct fit-up and root opening reduce the risk of incomplete root penetration and related discontinuities.

content.stem: Risk-based selection of which components to PMI typically prioritizes:
options: Only the exterior painted carbon-steel surfaces of components
Components chosen completely at random regardless of the service
Alloy components whose failure carries higher consequence
Items already fully covered by the vessel nameplate stamping data
content.explanation: A risk-based PMI plan focuses on alloy items where a mix-up would have higher failure consequence, rather than testing everything equally.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 305 methods for a damaged flange face may include which approach?
options: Painting the flange face to fill the damage
Raising the system pressure to reseat it
Removing the flange and leaving an open end
Refacing or weld-repairing the seating surface
content.explanation: Article 305 covers flange repair/conversion such as refacing or weld-repairing the gasket seating surface to restore a tight joint.

content.stem: A butt-welded insert plate (Article 201) is preferred over a fillet-welded patch mainly because it:
options: Provides a full-penetration, flush, permanent repair
Is faster to install with no welding required
Always raises the vessel rated MAWP value
Avoids the need for any post-repair examination
content.explanation: An insert plate gives a full-penetration, flush repair (essentially restoring base metal), unlike a lap/fillet patch which has more limitations.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 8.625 in, P = 600 psi, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness from t = PD/(2(SEW + PY))?
content.explanation: t = (600 x 8.625)/(2 x (20000 x 1.0 x 1.0 + 600 x 0.4)) = 0.1278 in. Dropping the PY term or using radius for D are the common errors.

content.stem: Straight pipe, OD D = 12.75 in, P = 720 psi, S = 18900 psi, E = 0.85 (ERW), W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness?
content.explanation: t = (720 x 12.75)/(2 x (18900 x 0.85 x 1.0 + 720 x 0.4)) = 0.2807 in. The 0.85 quality factor for ERW lowers the effective strength versus seamless.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 6.625 in, P = 500 psi, S = 17100 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness?
Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 10.75 in, measured wall t = 0.300 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Maximum internal pressure from P = 2tSEW/(D - 2Yt)?
Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 8.625 in, measured wall t = 0.250 in, S = 17100 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Maximum internal pressure?
options: 2079 psi

content.stem: A pipe's B31.3 pressure-design thickness is 0.182 in and a corrosion allowance of 0.100 in is specified. Required minimum thickness (t + c)?
content.explanation: Required minimum thickness = pressure-design thickness + allowances = 0.182 + 0.100 = 0.282 in.

content.stem: A piping CML read 0.432 in 10 years ago and reads 0.288 in today. Long-term corrosion rate?
content.explanation: Long-term rate = (t_initial - t_actual)/time = (0.432 - 0.288)/10 = 0.0144 in/yr.

content.stem: A CML read 0.337 in at the last inspection 4 years ago and reads 0.281 in now. Short-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.007 in/yr
0.028 in/yr
0.014 in/yr
content.explanation: Short-term rate = (t_previous - t_actual)/time = (0.337 - 0.281)/4 = 0.014 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.288 in, t_required = 0.140 in, corrosion rate = 0.0145 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 5.1 years
19.9 years
10.2 years
9.7 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.288 - 0.140)/0.0145 = 10.2 years.

content.stem: A piping circuit has a remaining life of 16 years. The maximum thickness-measurement interval for its piping class is 10 years. What inspection interval applies?
options: 5 years
16 years
10 years
8 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (8 yr) or the class maximum (10 yr); half-life governs at 8 years.

content.stem: A piping circuit has a remaining life of 24 years. The maximum thickness-measurement interval for its piping class is 10 years. What inspection interval applies?
options: 10 years
12 years
24 years
5 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (12 yr) or the class maximum (10 yr); the class maximum governs at 10 years.

content.stem: A vertical piping run has a design pressure of 150 psi at the top. A point is 80 ft lower (SG = 1.0). Total pressure at the lower point?
options: 150 psi
34.6 psi
content.explanation: Total = design pressure + static head = 150 + (0.433 x 80) = 184.6 psi.

content.stem: Two dissimilar metals are coupled in a conductive water-wetted joint and the less-noble metal corrodes preferentially. Which mechanism is this?
options: Mechanical fatigue cracking
Sulfidation of the steel
Galvanic corrosion
Microbiologically influenced corrosion
content.explanation: A dissimilar-metal couple in an electrolyte drives galvanic corrosion, with the less-noble (anodic) metal corroding faster.

content.stem: A primary way to mitigate galvanic corrosion at a dissimilar-metal piping connection is to:
options: Reduce the corrosion allowance on the anodic metal
Increase the line operating pressure to limit the flow
Paint only the more-noble metal at the connection
Electrically isolate the two metals with an insulating kit
content.explanation: Isolating the couple (insulating gaskets/sleeves) breaks the galvanic circuit; coatings and area ratios also matter, but isolation is the direct control.

content.stem: A small-bore branch connection at a reciprocating pump develops cracks after repeated cyclic loading and vibration. Which mechanism fits?
options: Soil-side external corrosion of the pipe
Galvanic corrosion at a dissimilar joint
Sulfidation thinning of the steel wall
Mechanical fatigue (vibration-induced)
content.explanation: Cyclic/vibratory stress concentrating at small-bore connections drives vibration-induced mechanical fatigue cracking.

content.stem: Vibration-induced fatigue in piping is most effectively reduced by:
options: Adding bracing or gusseting to lower cyclic stress at the connection
Raising the line operating temperature to relax the applied stress
Switching the inspection method from ultrasonics to radiography
Increasing the design corrosion allowance value on the run pipe
content.explanation: Stiffening/bracing small-bore connections reduces the cyclic stress amplitude that drives fatigue; good geometry at the branch also helps.

content.stem: Localized under-deposit pitting is found in a stagnant water-containing line, associated with biofilms and microbial activity. Which mechanism fits?
options: Microbiologically influenced corrosion
Galvanic corrosion at a dissimilar couple
Mechanical fatigue cracking from vibration
Sulfidation thinning of the steel wall
content.explanation: Microbial colonies and biofilms in stagnant, water-wetted conditions cause localized under-deposit pitting - MIC.

content.stem: Buried carbon-steel piping shows external metal loss that varies with soil moisture and resistivity. Which mechanism is indicated?
options: Sulfidation of the steel wall
Soil-side external corrosion
Galvanic corrosion of the bore
Mechanical fatigue cracking
content.explanation: External corrosion of buried piping driven by soil moisture, resistivity, and aeration is soil corrosion; the soil-to-air interface is a known hot spot.

content.stem: On buried piping, a location warranting particular inspection attention for external corrosion is:
options: The exact geometric center of any long straight buried section
The soil-to-air interface where the pipe enters or exits grade
The internal bore at a fully welded circumferential butt joint
The nameplate marking area on an adjacent above-grade vessel
content.explanation: The soil-to-air interface sees moisture and aeration changes and is a classic soil-corrosion hot spot.

content.stem: Carbon-steel piping in acidic sour water (H2S plus water, low pH) shows general and localized thinning. Which mechanism fits?
options: Mechanical fatigue cracking
Galvanic corrosion of the wall
Sour water corrosion (acidic)
Soil-side external corrosion
content.explanation: Acidic sour water (H2S-laden, low pH) corrodes carbon steel, with rate sensitive to pH, velocity, and H2S content.

content.stem: API 570 assigns piping to inspection classes primarily on the basis of:
options: The potential consequence of a leak or failure in the service
The exterior paint color scheme selected for the piping run
The number of welders who fabricated the spool pieces here
The brand of the valves that are installed in the circuit
content.explanation: Piping classes (e.g., Class 1 highest) are set by the consequence/risk of a release, which then drives inspection scope and intervals.

content.stem: A condition monitoring location (CML) on a piping circuit is:
options: A valve that must remain car-sealed in the open position in service
A designated site where inspection measurements are repeated over time
A welder qualification record that is retained in the piping file
A length of pipe that is exempt from all routine thickness monitoring
content.explanation: CMLs are fixed, designated sites where thickness/condition data are taken and trended across inspections.

content.stem: Injection points receive special inspection attention in API 570 because they:
options: Eliminate any need to inspect the remainder of the piping circuit run
Are always the single lowest-consequence part of any piping circuit
Cannot be monitored with ultrasonic thickness methods at all reliably
Experience accelerated, localized corrosion downstream of the injection
content.explanation: Turbulence and chemistry changes at injection points cause localized accelerated corrosion, so a defined upstream/downstream CML zone is monitored.

content.stem: Dead legs in piping warrant inspection attention chiefly because they:
options: Are fully exempt from the piping inspection program requirements
Always carry the very highest flow velocity in the whole circuit
Trap stagnant fluid or condensate that drives localized corrosion
Only affect the exterior coating and never the underlying metal
content.explanation: Stagnant fluid and condensate collect in dead legs, where localized corrosion (including MIC) can go undetected without targeted CMLs.

content.stem: Under API 570, a repair to in-service piping must be:
options: Authorized and carried out under inspector oversight with proper records
Completed verbally without any supporting documentation at all today
Performed only after first raising the piping design pressure rating
Limited to simply repainting the external pipe surface in that area
content.explanation: Repairs are authorized, performed to a recognized procedure under the inspector's oversight, and documented; temporary repairs are tracked until made permanent.

content.stem: A rerate of a piping system to new conditions under API 570 requires:
options: Only the informal verbal agreement of the operating shift personnel
An engineering evaluation confirming the new conditions are acceptable
Nothing beyond applying a fresh coat of external protective paint
An automatic reduction of the routine inspection frequency applied
content.explanation: A rerate (change in design T/P or rating) requires engineering review confirming the piping is suitable, with records and any needed testing.

content.stem: A temporary clamp or full-encirclement sleeve repair on in-service piping should be:
options: Installed without any evaluation of the defect it covers
Treated as a permanent repair needing no further tracking
Documented and re-inspected, then made permanent when practical
Used to raise the piping rated design pressure permanently
content.explanation: Temporary repairs are evaluated, documented, and monitored, and are replaced with a permanent repair at the next suitable opportunity.

content.stem: RP 574 guidance on selecting thickness-measurement locations emphasizes:
options: Locations chosen purely at random along the circuit
Only the straight runs farthest from any fitting or valve
The exterior paint condition rather than wall thickness
Components and geometries where higher metal loss is expected
content.explanation: RP 574 directs TMLs/CMLs toward fittings, elbows, tees, and turbulence/erosion-prone geometries where loss concentrates.

content.stem: RP 574 notes that small-bore and auxiliary piping deserve attention because they:
options: Are easily overlooked yet can fail from corrosion or fatigue
Always carry the lowest consequence in any process unit
Never connect to the main pressure-containing piping run
Are exempt from the owner's piping inspection program
content.explanation: Small-bore/auxiliary connections are commonly under-inspected but fail from corrosion, fatigue, or mechanical damage.

content.stem: The pressure-temperature rating of a B16.5 flange depends on which combination?
options: The exterior paint color and the bolt vendor
The flange class, material group, and temperature
The welder identity and the fabrication date
The line corrosion allowance and the pipe length
content.explanation: B16.5 rates a flange by its class (e.g., 150/300/600), its material group, and the operating temperature, read from the pressure-temperature rating tables.

content.stem: For a given material group, increasing the operating temperature of a B16.5 flange generally:
options: Has no effect on the pressure rating
Raises its allowable pressure rating
Lowers its allowable pressure rating
Eliminates the need for a gasket
content.explanation: Allowable pressure falls as temperature rises because material strength decreases; the rating tables capture this for each class and material group.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 501 addresses which activity for piping and equipment?
options: Assignment of the piping inspection class
Qualification of welders for the repair
Selection of the exterior coating system
Pressure and tightness testing of the system
content.explanation: Article 501 covers pressure and tightness testing methods used to verify integrity of piping and equipment.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 502 provides for which alternative during repairs or alterations?
options: NDE in lieu of a pressure test where testing is impractical
Skipping all examination of the completed repair weld
Raising the system rating without any evaluation
Replacing the inspector's role with an operator sign-off
content.explanation: Article 502 allows qualified NDE as an alternative to pressure testing when a pressure test is not practical for the repair or alteration.

content.stem: A full-encirclement steel reinforcing sleeve (Article 206) is used on piping mainly to:
options: Increase the internal diameter of the run pipe substantially
Restore or reinforce a corroded or defective pipe section
Lower the design pressure rating of the piping system run
Remove the need for any future inspection at that location
content.explanation: A full-encirclement sleeve reinforces or contains a defective section; design must address the defect, loads, and whether it is pressure-containing.

content.stem: A mechanical clamp repair (Article 306) on piping is generally regarded as:
options: A method used to permanently rerate the piping system upward
A permanent repair that needs no further inspection at all
A temporary repair that is monitored until a permanent fix
A direct substitute for qualifying the repair welders used
content.explanation: Bolted mechanical clamps are typically temporary repairs, evaluated for the service and monitored until replaced by a permanent repair.

content.stem: Liquid penetrant examination (Article 6) detects discontinuities that are:
options: Open to the surface in nonporous materials
Buried deep within the base metal volume
Only present in ferromagnetic materials
Visible only on a radiographic film image
content.explanation: PT reveals surface-breaking discontinuities in nonporous materials via penetrant, removal, and developer; it cannot find subsurface flaws.

content.stem: Magnetic particle examination (Article 7) is applicable to:
options: Only volumetric examination of relatively thick steel castings
Deeply buried volumetric flaws in austenitic stainless piping
Any nonmagnetic material regardless of the specific alloy used
Surface and slightly subsurface flaws in ferromagnetic materials
content.explanation: MT detects surface and near-surface discontinuities in ferromagnetic materials by magnetizing the part and applying particles; it does not work on nonmagnetic alloys.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 4.500 in, P = 850 psi, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness from t = PD/(2(SEW + PY))?
Straight pipe, OD D = 16.0 in, P = 400 psi, S = 16700 psi, E = 0.85 (ERW), W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness?
content.explanation: t = (400 x 16.0)/(2 x (16700 x 0.85 x 1.0 + 400 x 0.4)) = 0.2229 in. The 0.85 ERW quality factor reduces the effective strength versus seamless pipe.

content.stem: New pipe is specified with a nominal wall of 0.322 in. Allowing the 12.5% pipe mill under-tolerance, what is the minimum wall that could be supplied?
content.explanation: Minimum supplied wall = nominal x (1 - 0.125) = 0.322 x 0.875 = 0.2818 in. The 12.5% under-tolerance must be considered when setting starting thickness for new piping.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 6.625 in, measured wall t = 0.220 in, S = 18900 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Maximum internal pressure from P = 2tSEW/(D - 2Yt)?
Per ASME B31.3, the minimum hydrostatic leak-test pressure is 1.5 times the design pressure (equal test and design temperatures). For a piping design pressure of 300 psi, what is it?
options: 390 psi
450 psi
330 psi
300 psi
content.explanation: Hydrostatic leak-test pressure = 1.5 x design pressure = 1.5 x 300 = 450 psi (equal test and design temperatures). When they differ, B31.3 345.4.2 multiplies by the stress ratio S_test/S_design (capped). B31.3 uses 1.5x for piping, higher than the 1.3x for ASME VIII-1 vessels.

content.stem: A piping system has a design pressure of 450 psi. Using the B31.3 1.5x factor (equal test and design temperatures), the minimum hydrostatic test pressure is:
options: 450 psi
585 psi
675 psi
content.explanation: Minimum hydrostatic test pressure = 1.5 x design pressure = 1.5 x 450 = 675 psi (equal test and design temperatures; a stress-ratio correction per 345.4.2 applies when they differ).

content.stem: A CML measured 0.300 in eight years ago and 0.220 in today. The long-term corrosion rate is:
options: 0.01 in/yr
0.02 in/yr
0.005 in/yr
content.explanation: Long-term rate = (t_initial - t_actual)/time = (0.300 - 0.220)/8 = 0.01 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.220 in, t_required = 0.125 in, corrosion rate = 0.010 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 9.5 years
22 years
4.8 years
12.5 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.220 - 0.125)/0.010 = 9.5 years.

content.stem: A circuit has a long-term rate of 0.008 in/yr and a short-term rate of 0.014 in/yr. Using the more conservative rate with t_actual = 0.260 in and t_required = 0.120 in, the remaining life is:
options: 17.5 years
10 years
6.4 years
18.6 years
content.explanation: The more conservative (higher) rate, 0.014 in/yr, gives the shorter remaining life: (0.260 - 0.120)/0.014 = 10 years.

content.stem: A piping circuit has a remaining life of 9 years. The class maximum thickness-measurement interval is 10 years. What interval applies?
options: 9 years
4.5 years
10 years
5 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (4.5 yr) or the class maximum (10 yr); half-life governs at 4.5 years.

content.stem: A vertical line has a design pressure of 200 psi at the top. A point sits 120 ft below (SG = 1.0). Total pressure at that point?
options: 52 psi
200 psi
252 psi
148 psi
content.explanation: Total = design pressure + static head = 200 + (0.433 x 120) = 252 psi.

content.stem: External visual inspection of piping under API 570 is scheduled primarily on the basis of:
options: The total number of flanges present in the circuit
The exterior paint gloss measured at the last shutdown
The piping class and the likelihood of external degradation
The brand of insulation jacketing on the piping run
content.explanation: External inspection intervals follow the piping class and the credible external mechanisms (e.g., CUI, atmospheric, soil-side), not cosmetic factors.

content.stem: API 570 calls for targeted inspection for corrosion under insulation chiefly in:
options: Only the fully buried underground sections of the piping circuit
The susceptible temperature range where insulation traps moisture
Lines that operate continuously above 1000 F in dry service
Bare, uninsulated indoor piping kept in dry ambient service
content.explanation: CUI inspection targets insulated carbon steel in the susceptible temperature band where moisture is trapped against the wall, plus damaged-jacket and dripping locations.

content.stem: For buried piping, API 570 relies on which approach to manage external corrosion?
options: Cathodic protection monitoring plus periodic condition assessment
Only an annual external repaint of any above-grade exposed sections
Raising the internal design pressure to offset the external metal loss
Ignoring the buried run entirely because soil cannot corrode steel
content.explanation: Buried piping integrity uses cathodic protection (with CP surveys), coating assessment, and soil-to-air interface checks or excavation as warranted.

content.stem: After a repair or alteration, API 570 generally expects a pressure test unless:
options: A code-recognized NDE alternative is applied and documented
The operating crew agrees verbally to skip the test
The repair was simply a fresh coat of external paint
The piping was repainted to match the surrounding lines
content.explanation: A pressure test is normally performed after repairs/alterations; NDE in lieu (e.g., PCC-2 502) may substitute where a test is impractical, with proper documentation.

content.stem: On-stream inspection of piping is valuable mainly because it:
options: Applies only to piping lines that have already been retired
Permanently removes the need for any future turnaround inspection
Raises the rated design pressure of the whole piping system run
Allows monitoring of conditions while the line remains in service
content.explanation: On-stream techniques (e.g., UT, RT profile) let inspectors track thinning and other damage without taking the line out of service.

content.stem: Threaded and small-bore connections receive special attention because they are:
options: Fully exempt from the owner-user piping inspection program scope
Always the single highest-pressure component in any piping circuit
Prone to fatigue, corrosion, and mechanical damage yet easily missed
Made only from corrosion-resistant alloys as a strict code rule
content.explanation: Small-bore/threaded connections concentrate stress and corrode locally; they fail more than their size suggests and are deliberately included in the plan.

content.stem: The required minimum thickness for in-service piping is governed by:
options: The nominal pipe schedule alone with no other consideration at all
Only the exterior coating thickness applied over the bare pipe wall
Whichever single value the operator happens to find convenient
The greater of the pressure-design and structural-minimum thickness
content.explanation: Minimum thickness must satisfy both pressure-design (B31.3) and a structural minimum; the larger governs.

content.stem: API 570 requires the owner-user to maintain piping inspection records that include:
options: Only the names of the operators who were on shift that day
Inspection results, thickness data, and the basis for intervals
Solely the exterior paint batch numbers and the color codes used
Just the daily lunch schedule kept for the inspection crew members
content.explanation: Records document inspection results, CML thickness data, corrosion rates, remaining life, and the interval basis, supporting the integrity program.

content.stem: ASME B31.3 Chapter V addresses which aspect of piping welds?
options: The brand of the welding machine used on the job
The exterior paint system applied over the finished weld
Joint types, weld sizes, and preheat or heat-treatment rules
The lunch breaks taken by the welders during the shift
content.explanation: Chapter V covers welding details: joint geometry, weld sizes, restrictions, allowable reinforcement, inspection, and preheat/PWHT requirements.

content.stem: Whether postweld heat treatment is required for a B31.3 weld depends chiefly on:
options: The exterior color of the finished pipe coating
The material group and the thickness being welded
The total number of welders on the project crew
The brand of filler metal used for the weld pass
content.explanation: PWHT requirements in B31.3 are driven by the material (P-number-like grouping) and thickness, with tabulated rules.

content.stem: Where API 570 gives a welding rule that differs from ASME B31.3 on the same point, which governs?
options: API 570, whose rules take precedence over B31.3 on that point
ASME B31.3, which always overrides API 570 entirely on the point
