Neither one, since the two never address the very same point
Whichever document the welder personally happens to prefer
content.explanation: Per the API 570 BoK, rules for welding given in API 570 take precedence over those covering the same areas in ASME B31.3.

content.stem: RP 574 notes that at elbows and tees, thickness readings should concentrate on:
options: The outer radius and other erosion-prone geometry
Only the straight tangent far from the fitting
The exterior paint rather than the pipe wall
Locations chosen purely at random on the fitting
content.explanation: Flow turbulence at elbow extrados and tee branches accelerates erosion/erosion-corrosion, so TMLs concentrate there.

content.stem: RP 574 lists which method as a common means of measuring piping wall thickness on-stream?
options: Magnetic particle examination
Ultrasonic thickness measurement
Liquid penetrant examination
Visual examination of the coating
content.explanation: Ultrasonic thickness gauging is a primary on-stream wall-measurement method; RT profile is another. MT and PT find surface flaws, not wall loss.

content.stem: RP 576 identifies which condition as a common cause of relief-valve malfunction?
options: Routine bench testing performed at the proper interval
Correctly applied car-seals on the inlet block valve
Corrosion, fouling, or deposits on the valve internals
An adequately sized and unobstructed discharge line
content.explanation: Corrosion, fouling, and deposits on seats/springs are frequent causes of PRD failure to function as intended.

content.stem: RP 576 indicates that the set pressure of a relief device is verified by:
options: Counting the bolts on the valve body flange
Reading the exterior nameplate color of the valve
Measuring the discharge pipe outside diameter
Bench testing (pop testing) at the prescribed interval
content.explanation: Pop/bench testing confirms the device opens at its set pressure; intervals are risk- and history-based.

content.stem: An isolation (block) valve in a relief-device inlet line must be managed so that it:
options: Stays locked or car-sealed open to keep relief available
Remains closed to protect the valve from process fouling
Replaces the requirement to bench-test the relief device
Sets the relief device opening pressure during operation
content.explanation: Block valves on relief paths are car-sealed/locked open under administrative control so the relief path is never inadvertently isolated.

content.stem: RP 577 describes the relationship among welding documents as:
options: The WPS replaces the need for any welder qualification
The PQR supports the WPS, and the WPQ qualifies the welder
The WPQ is written before any procedure qualification test
The PQR is optional whenever a WPS already exists
content.explanation: A qualified WPS is supported by a PQR (test record), and the welder is separately qualified by a WPQ.

content.stem: Which is a weld discontinuity an inspector evaluates against acceptance criteria?
options: The welder's certification expiration date
The exterior paint sheen over the finished weld
Incomplete fusion between the weld and base metal
The brand name printed on the filler metal spool
content.explanation: Incomplete fusion, porosity, slag, undercut, and cracks are weld discontinuities judged against the code's acceptance criteria.

content.stem: RP 578's material verification program exists primarily to prevent:
options: Selection of an oversized relief-valve discharge piping line
Application of an incorrect exterior paint color on the line
Use of an expired welder qualification record on the project
Installation of an incorrect alloy in a critical service
content.explanation: PMI verifies that the alloy actually installed matches the specification, guarding against material mix-ups that can fail in service.

content.stem: ASME Section IX assigns P-Numbers to base metals in order to:
options: Fix the discharge line size of the relief device that is used
Set the exterior paint color used for each material grade
Define the daily lunch schedule for the assigned welding crew
Group similar materials to reduce the number of qualifications
content.explanation: P-Numbers group base metals with similar characteristics so one qualification can cover a range, reducing redundant testing.

content.stem: A change in an essential variable on a welding procedure requires:
options: A repaint of the welded component surface
Only an edit to the document revision block
Requalification of the WPS with a new PQR
No action because all variables are optional
content.explanation: Changing an essential variable affects mechanical properties and requires requalification (supported by a new PQR).

content.stem: The purpose of a Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) is to:
options: Provide qualified direction for making a production weld
Record only the welder's personal performance test results
List the exterior coatings applied after the welding is done
Document the relief-valve set-pressure history for the line
content.explanation: A WPS gives the qualified parameters for production welding; it is supported by a PQR and is distinct from welder performance qualification.

content.stem: A B16.5 flange class designation (for example 150 or 300) primarily indicates the flange's:
options: Pressure-temperature rating capability for its material
Exterior paint color applied at the fabrication shop
Required liquid penetrant examination frequency
Nominal corrosion allowance built into the casting
content.explanation: The class (150/300/600/...) indexes the pressure-temperature rating; the actual allowable pressure depends on class, material group, and temperature.

content.stem: A leaking flanged joint inspected under the piping program is most directly evaluated for:
options: The exterior color match of the two pipe runs
Gasket condition, bolt load, and flange-face integrity
The welder qualification used elsewhere on the line
The relief device set pressure on a separate circuit
content.explanation: A leaking flange is assessed for gasket seating, bolt torque/load, and flange-face/seating-surface condition; PCC-2 305 covers face repair.

content.stem: Acidic sour water corrosion of carbon steel is distinguished from alkaline sour water by:
options: Its dependence on the exterior coating color applied to the pipe
Its complete absence of any dissolved hydrogen sulfide content
Its strict requirement for fully buried piping to occur at all
Its low pH, which drives more aggressive general and localized loss
content.explanation: Acidic sour water (low pH, H2S-laden) is more corrosive to carbon steel than alkaline sour water; rate rises with H2S, velocity, and falling pH.

content.stem: A practical mitigation for microbiologically influenced corrosion in piping is to:
options: Repaint the external pipe surface on a fixed schedule
Raise the system pressure to crush the microbes present
Reduce stagnation and control biocide treatment of the fluid
Increase the flange bolt torque at each connection
content.explanation: MIC is controlled by limiting stagnation/deposits, maintaining flow, cleaning, and biocide treatment of the process or water.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 10.75 in, P = 650 psi, S = 17100 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness from t = PD/(2(SEW + PY))?
Straight pipe, OD D = 20.0 in, P = 350 psi, S = 20000 psi, E = 0.85 (ERW), W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness?
Straight seamless pipe at elevated temperature: D = 8.625 in, P = 500 psi, S = 14000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 0.95 (weld strength reduction), Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness?
content.explanation: t = (500 x 8.625)/(2 x (14000 x 1.0 x 0.95 + 500 x 0.4)) = 0.1597 in. The weld-strength-reduction factor W below 1.0 increases the required thickness at creep-range temperatures.

content.stem: A B31.3 blank (blind): gasket-load diameter d_g = 12.0 in, P = 300 psi, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0. Pressure-design thickness from t = d_g x sqrt(3P/(16SE))?
content.explanation: t = 12.0 x sqrt((3 x 300)/(16 x 20000 x 1.0)) = 0.6364 in, before adding allowances. Dropping the factor of 3, or using radius for d_g, are the common errors.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 12.75 in, measured wall t = 0.330 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Maximum internal pressure from P = 2tSEW/(D - 2Yt)?
options: 2160 psi

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 3.500 in, measured wall t = 0.180 in, S = 17100 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Maximum internal pressure?
A CML read 0.500 in twelve years ago and reads 0.350 in today. Long-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.025 in/yr
content.explanation: Long-term rate = (t_initial - t_actual)/time = (0.500 - 0.350)/12 = 0.0125 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.350 in, t_required = 0.150 in, corrosion rate = 0.0125 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 28 years
16 years
8 years
12 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.350 - 0.150)/0.0125 = 16 years.

content.stem: A piping circuit has a remaining life of 11 years. The class maximum thickness-measurement interval is 5 years. What inspection interval applies?
options: 2.5 years
5.5 years
11 years
5 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (5.5 yr) or the class maximum (5 yr); the class maximum governs at 5 years.

content.stem: Per ASME B31.3, with equal test and design temperatures, the minimum hydrostatic leak-test pressure for a 525 psi design pressure is:
options: 525 psi
content.explanation: Minimum hydrostatic test pressure = 1.5 x design pressure = 1.5 x 525 = 787.5 psi (equal test and design temperatures).

content.stem: For an in-service pipe, the pressure-design thickness is 0.165 in and the structural-minimum thickness is 0.220 in. Which value governs the required minimum thickness?
content.explanation: Required minimum thickness is the greater of pressure-design and structural minimum, so 0.220 in governs at 0.22 in.

content.stem: The number and placement of CMLs on a piping circuit should be based on:
options: The exterior paint area of the piping being inspected
A fixed count applied identically to every piping circuit
The expected type and location of the damage in that circuit
The total count of support shoes along the pipe rack
content.explanation: CML coverage is set by the anticipated damage type and location (e.g., injection points, elbows, dead legs), not a one-size count.

content.stem: Postponing a due piping inspection beyond its established interval generally requires:
options: Only an informal verbal nod from the operating shift supervisor
A documented engineering assessment justifying the deferral
Nothing at all, since intervals in API 570 are merely advisory
An automatic rerate of the piping to a much lower pressure rating
content.explanation: Deferral past a due date is supported by a documented assessment (often RBI- or condition-based), not an informal decision.

content.stem: When a risk-based inspection approach sets piping intervals, the interval is driven by:
options: Only the fixed calendar maximum regardless of any assessed risk
The likelihood and consequence of failure for that circuit
The exterior coating color that was chosen for the piping circuit
The number of inspectors who happen to be available that quarter
content.explanation: RBI sets intervals from the assessed probability and consequence of failure; it can extend or shorten relative to the default class interval.

content.stem: The MAWP of an in-service piping component is determined using:
options: The current measured thickness less the future corrosion loss
The original nominal thickness with no allowance for loss
The exterior insulation thickness over the component
Whichever pressure the operator finds most convenient
content.explanation: MAWP uses the actual thickness minus the loss expected before the next inspection, applied in the B31.3 pressure equation.

content.stem: Piping in vibrating or cyclic service warrants added attention to:
options: Fatigue cracking at branch connections and stress risers
Only the uniform general thinning of the straight run
Just the legibility of the line identification tag
Solely the exterior coating over the pipe surface
content.explanation: Vibration/cyclic loading drives fatigue at small-bore branches, supports, and other discontinuities, which the plan should target.

content.stem: A full-penetration insert (flush) patch in a pipe wall is generally preferred over a lap patch because it:
options: It requires no welding procedure qualification of any kind
It avoids the need for any post-repair examination at all
It always raises the rated pressure of the whole piping run
Restores the wall as a permanent, full-penetration repair
content.explanation: A flush insert restores base-metal continuity as a permanent repair; lap/fillet patches have more limitations and are often temporary.

content.stem: A temporary repair on in-service piping should be:
options: Used to permanently increase the piping design rating
Treated as permanent and removed from the tracking list
Left in place indefinitely without any further review
Tracked and replaced with a permanent repair when practical
content.explanation: Temporary repairs (clamps, sleeves, lap patches) are documented, monitored, and converted to permanent repairs at the next suitable opportunity.

content.stem: Under API 570, the authorized piping inspector is primarily responsible for:
options: Setting the corporate operating budget for the inspection group
Personally performing every single weld on a given repair job
Ensuring inspection, examination, and testing meet the code
Operating the process unit itself during normal production runs
content.explanation: The inspector ensures the integrity program's inspection, NDE, and testing comply with API 570; examiners perform the NDE under that oversight.

content.stem: When CUI is found at one location on an insulated circuit, API 570 guidance is to:
options: Expand inspection to other similar susceptible locations
Assume the rest of the circuit is unaffected and stop
Repaint only the single location that was inspected
Immediately retire the entire piping circuit from service
content.explanation: Finding CUI at one point prompts expanding the sample to other similar at-risk locations, since the mechanism is usually systemic.

content.stem: B31.3 branch-connection reinforcement is based on the principle that:
options: No additional metal is ever needed anywhere around an opening
The branch is always larger in diameter than the run pipe
Metal removed for the opening is replaced within a defined zone
The exterior protective coating provides the reinforcement
content.explanation: Area-replacement reinforcement requires the pressure-carrying metal removed by the opening to be replaced by available metal within the reinforcement zone.

content.stem: A mitered bend in B31.3 piping is treated specially because the miter joints:
options: Carry higher local stress than a smooth elbow of the same size
Are always stronger than a equivalent smooth-radius elbow
Require no pressure-design consideration of any kind
Eliminate the need to inspect the bend for thinning
content.explanation: Miter joints concentrate stress and have pressure-design rules (304.2.3) reflecting the angle and spacing of the cuts.

content.stem: A blank (blind) used to isolate piping is sized for pressure using a relationship that depends on:
options: Only the exterior protective paint thickness applied to the blank
The gasket-load diameter, pressure, allowable stress, and quality factor
The number of bolts present in the mating flange and nothing else
The length of the upstream piping run leading up to the blank
content.explanation: Blank thickness from 304.5.3 scales with the gasket diameter and the square root of P/(S E), plus allowances.

content.stem: B31.3 permits using standard flanges from a listed standard when:
options: They are installed without any gasket placed between the faces
They are painted to closely match the connecting pipe run colour
The operator simply prefers them to a calculated custom design
Their pressure-temperature rating covers the design conditions
content.explanation: Standard (listed) flanges are acceptable when their pressure-temperature rating, per the listed standard such as B16.5, covers the service.

content.stem: RP 574 notes that valve bodies in corrosive service should be inspected because they:
options: Never contain any pressure once installed in a line
Are exempt from thickness monitoring by code rule
Can thin at the body, seats, and flow-turbulence areas
Only matter for their exterior nameplate markings
content.explanation: Valve bodies thin from corrosion and erosion at the body, seats, and turbulent regions, and are included in the thickness program.

content.stem: RP 574 highlights bellows expansion joints as needing attention because they:
options: They only affect the exterior insulation jacketing of the line
They carry no pressure and require no inspection at all ever
They are always somewhat thicker than the adjoining pipe wall
Are thin-walled and prone to fatigue and corrosion damage
content.explanation: Thin-walled bellows flex in service and are vulnerable to fatigue, corrosion, and mechanical damage, warranting focused inspection.

content.stem: Sample and drain connections deserve inspection attention in RP 574 mainly because they:
options: Combine small-bore geometry with intermittent, aggressive flow
They are the single largest-diameter components in any circuit
They never see any process fluid once the line is in service
They are fully exempt from the piping inspection program scope
content.explanation: Small-bore sample/drain connections see intermittent, sometimes aggressive flow and concentrate corrosion and mechanical damage.

content.stem: RP 574 indicates the frequency of thickness readings at a component should increase when:
options: The exterior paint is a darker color than usual
The measured corrosion rate or consequence is higher
The component is farther from the control room
The line has more flanges than the average circuit
content.explanation: Higher measured corrosion rate or higher consequence warrants more frequent monitoring at that component.

content.stem: The inspection interval for a pressure-relief device under RP 576 is set primarily by:
options: The number of bolts on the discharge flange
The exterior paint color of the valve body
Its service history, fouling tendency, and risk
The length of the inlet piping nozzle run
content.explanation: PRD test/inspection intervals are based on service severity, past performance/fouling, and risk, not fixed cosmetic factors.

content.stem: Excessive inlet-line pressure loss to a relief valve can cause:
options: A larger corrosion allowance on the protected vessel
A permanent increase in the protected design pressure
Elimination of the need to bench-test the valve
Valve chatter that damages the seat and reduces capacity
content.explanation: Inlet pressure loss above about 3% can cause chatter, seat damage, and loss of effective relieving capacity.

content.stem: Preheat is applied before welding primarily to:
options: Slow cooling and reduce the risk of hydrogen cracking
Improve the exterior paint adhesion after welding
Shorten the welder's qualification test duration
Eliminate the need for any postweld examination
content.explanation: Preheat lowers cooling rate and drives off moisture, reducing hardening and hydrogen-induced cracking in susceptible steels.

content.stem: Which is correctly described as a linear weld discontinuity assessed against acceptance criteria?
options: The welder's expired qualification card
A crack running along the weld toe
The exterior paint sheen on the weld
The brand stamped on the filler spool
content.explanation: Cracks (including toe cracks) are linear discontinuities judged against the code's acceptance limits; rounded indications like porosity are non-linear.

content.stem: ASME Section IX F-Numbers group filler metals in order to:
options: Reduce the number of welder qualifications required
Set the exterior paint color for each weld pass
Define the discharge size of a relief device
Fix the lunch schedule for the welding crew
content.explanation: F-Numbers group filler metals by usability so a welder qualified with one is qualified for others in the group, reducing redundant testing.

content.stem: Qualifying a welder on pipe in the 6G position is significant because it:
options: Covers only the exact 6G orientation and nothing else
Covers all positions due to its combined difficulty
Applies solely to plate and never to pipe welds
Is the easiest welding position to qualify in
content.explanation: The 6G (inclined, fixed) position combines several orientations, so qualifying in it covers all positions within the applicable scope.

content.stem: The thickness range a welder is qualified to deposit is governed in Section IX by:
options: The number of flanges on the finished line
The exterior coating applied after welding
The thickness of the test coupon they welded
The brand of the welding power supply used
content.explanation: Qualified deposit thickness range is set by the test-coupon thickness per the QW-451/452 rules.

content.stem: The flange facing type (e.g., raised face vs ring-type joint) chiefly affects:
options: The welder qualification used on the line
The exterior paint color of the flange
How the gasket seats and seals the joint
The relief device set pressure downstream
content.explanation: Facing type (RF, RTJ, flat face) determines gasket type and how the joint seals; it must match the mating flange.

content.stem: Adequate and uniform bolt load on a B16.5 flanged joint is important because it:
options: Fixes the relief valve set pressure on the line
Sets the pipe wall corrosion allowance value
Determines the pipe nominal schedule number
Maintains gasket seating and a leak-tight seal
content.explanation: Uniform, adequate bolt load seats the gasket and keeps the joint tight; uneven or low load leads to leaks.

content.stem: A water-drawoff line that sits idle for long periods develops localized pitting under deposits with evidence of biological activity. Which mechanism fits?
options: Microbiologically influenced corrosion
Galvanic corrosion at a dissimilar metal couple
Mechanical fatigue cracking from line vibration
Soil-side external corrosion of the buried pipe
content.explanation: Stagnant, water-wetted, deposit-laden conditions with biofilms point to MIC, often as localized under-deposit pitting.

content.stem: A coated buried transfer line shows external metal loss concentrated where the coating is damaged and the soil stays moist. Which mechanism fits?
options: Microbiologically influenced corrosion
Soil-side external corrosion
Galvanic corrosion of the bore
Mechanical fatigue cracking
content.explanation: External loss at coating holidays in moist soil is soil corrosion; coating condition and cathodic protection govern the rate.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 14.0 in, P = 480 psi, S = 18900 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness from t = PD/(2(SEW + PY))?
Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 2.375 in, P = 900 psi, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness?
An in-service seamless pipe has OD D = 8.625 in and a current measured wall t = 0.280 in. With S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4, the MAWP from P = 2tSEW/(D - 2Yt) is:
content.explanation: MAWP = (2 x 0.280 x 20000 x 1.0 x 1.0)/(8.625 - 2 x 0.4 x 0.280) = 1333.2 psi, using the current measured wall.

content.stem: An in-service seamless pipe has OD D = 6.625 in. The measured wall is 0.245 in but 0.020 in of loss is expected before the next inspection. With S = 17100 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4, the MAWP based on the future thickness (0.225 in) is:
content.explanation: MAWP uses the thickness expected before the next inspection: t = 0.245 - 0.020 = 0.225 in, so MAWP = (2 x 0.225 x 17100)/(6.625 - 2 x 0.4 x 0.225) = 1193.9 psi.

content.stem: A pipe's B31.3 pressure-design thickness is 0.146 in and a 0.085 in corrosion allowance is specified. Required minimum thickness (t + c)?
content.explanation: Required minimum thickness = pressure-design thickness + corrosion allowance = 0.146 + 0.085 = 0.231 in.

content.stem: A CML measured 0.365 in at the last inspection 5 years ago and 0.300 in now. Short-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.026 in/yr
0.013 in/yr
0.073 in/yr
content.explanation: Short-term rate = (t_previous - t_actual)/time = (0.365 - 0.300)/5 = 0.013 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.300 in, t_required = 0.180 in, corrosion rate = 0.013 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 13.8 years
23.1 years
4.6 years
9.2 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.300 - 0.180)/0.013 = 9.2 years.

content.stem: A piping circuit has a remaining life of 7 years. The class maximum thickness-measurement interval is 10 years. What inspection interval applies?
options: 5 years
7 years
10 years
3.5 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (3.5 yr) or the class maximum (10 yr); half-life governs at 3.5 years.

content.stem: Per ASME B31.3, with equal test and design temperatures, the minimum hydrostatic leak-test pressure for a 240 psi design pressure is:
options: 264 psi
312 psi
360 psi
240 psi
content.explanation: Minimum hydrostatic test pressure = 1.5 x design pressure = 1.5 x 240 = 360 psi (equal test and design temperatures).

content.stem: Per ASME B31.3, the pneumatic leak-test pressure is 1.1 times the design pressure. For a 300 psi design pressure, the pneumatic test pressure is:
options: 390 psi
450 psi
330 psi
300 psi
content.explanation: Pneumatic test pressure = 1.1 x design pressure = 1.1 x 300 = 330 psi. B31.3 uses a lower factor for pneumatic than the 1.5x hydrostatic because of the greater stored energy in a gas test.

content.stem: Radiographic examination under Article 2 is best suited to detecting which kind of flaw?
options: Only fine surface-breaking cracks in a nonporous coating layer
Volumetric flaws such as porosity, slag, and incomplete penetration
Solely the exterior paint thickness applied over the finished weld
Just the welder qualification status recorded for the joint
content.explanation: RT is a volumetric method that images porosity, slag, and incomplete penetration/fusion; tight surface cracks can be missed if poorly oriented.

content.stem: In radiographic examination, the image quality indicator (penetrameter) is used to:
options: Measure the exterior protective coating thickness over the welded joint
Set the relief device opening pressure on the connected piping line
Demonstrate that the radiographic technique has adequate sensitivity
Record the welder performance qualification expiration date for the joint
content.explanation: The IQI (hole or wire type) verifies the radiograph shows the required sensitivity to detect small discontinuities.

content.stem: Radiographic film density requirements in Article 2 exist to ensure that:
options: The welder used a specific brand of covered electrode filler rod
The exterior protective paint on the pipe dries within a set dwell time
The bolts on the nearest mating flange are torqued to a fixed value
The image has enough contrast and latitude to reveal discontinuities
content.explanation: Density (and contrast) limits keep the radiograph readable so real discontinuities are not masked by under- or over-exposure.

content.stem: Direct visual examination under Article 9 typically requires which condition to be controlled?
options: Adequate illumination and access to the surface being viewed
A specific brand of penetrant applied before the viewing
Magnetization of the part before the inspector looks at it
A radiographic film exposure taken of the same area first
content.explanation: Visual examination depends on adequate lighting, viewing angle/distance, and access; aids like mirrors or borescopes extend it to remote areas.

content.stem: Remote visual examination (Article 9) is used when:
options: The part must first be magnetized to reveal flaws
Direct line of sight to the surface is not practical
A penetrant dwell time has just been completed
The exterior coating color needs to be matched
content.explanation: Remote VT (borescopes, cameras, mirrors) substitutes for direct viewing where access or line of sight is limited, with equivalent resolution required.

content.stem: Leak testing under Article 10 is used to detect:
options: The welder qualification record for the joint made
Subsurface volumetric flaws deep within the base metal
The exterior paint adhesion over the welded joint
Through-thickness leakage paths in the pressure boundary
content.explanation: LT (bubble, pressure-change, halogen, helium) finds through-wall leak paths rather than embedded flaws.

content.stem: A bubble-test leak examination (Article 10) reveals a leak by:
options: Forming bubbles where pressurized gas escapes through a defect
Producing an indication on a radiographic film image
Magnetizing the part to attract iron particles to the flaw
Measuring the exterior coating thickness over the seam
content.explanation: In a bubble test, gas escaping a through-leak forms bubbles in the solution, marking the leak location.

content.stem: RP 574 supports trending CML thickness data over time chiefly to:
options: Record the exterior paint batch used on the line
Establish corrosion rates and project remaining life
Set the relief device discharge pipe diameter
Document the daily shift schedule of inspectors
content.explanation: Trending repeated CML readings yields corrosion rates, which drive remaining-life and interval decisions.

content.stem: RP 574 flags threaded piping connections as higher-risk because they:
options: Carry no internal pressure once installed in the line
Are always made of corrosion-resistant alloy by rule
Concentrate stress at the threads and lose section there
Only affect the exterior insulation jacket of the pipe
content.explanation: Threads reduce the load-bearing section and concentrate stress, making threaded joints prone to fatigue and corrosion failure.

content.stem: RP 574 notes that radiographic profile (RT) thickness checks are useful where:
options: The relief valve set pressure must be re-established on the connected line
The exterior paint must be carefully matched to the adjacent piping run
A welder performance qualification record needs to be verified on site
Direct ultrasonic contact is impractical, such as under insulation
content.explanation: RT profiling images the wall without removing insulation/contacting the surface, complementing ultrasonic gauging where contact is hard.

content.stem: RP 574 recommends a defined monitoring zone around an injection point that extends:
options: Upstream and downstream to capture the accelerated-corrosion region
Only to the single weld nearest the injection nozzle fitting itself
Across the entire process unit regardless of where the injection occurs
Solely over the exterior protective coating near the injection fitting
content.explanation: The injection-point circuit covers a defined upstream/downstream zone where turbulence and chemistry change accelerate corrosion.

content.stem: A conventional spring-loaded pressure-relief valve differs from a balanced-bellows type mainly in:
options: The exterior protective paint color applied to the valve body casting
Its sensitivity of set pressure to superimposed backpressure
The number of bolts that are used on the valve inlet flange joint
The brand of the gasket fitted at the valve outlet flange joint
content.explanation: A conventional PRV's opening is affected by backpressure, while a balanced-bellows design compensates for it.

content.stem: RP 576 inspection of a removed relief valve includes checking the:
options: Welder qualification used elsewhere on the same process unit run
Exterior paint gloss measured at the unit's last scheduled shutdown
Seat, spring, and internal surfaces for corrosion or fouling
Corrosion allowance of the protected pressure vessel shell course
content.explanation: A bench inspection examines the seat, disc, spring, and internals for corrosion, fouling, and damage that would impair function.

content.stem: When a relief valve fails to open at its set pressure during a bench test, the appropriate action is to:
options: Repaint the valve body casing and reinstall it without any retesting
Return it to service unchanged, since bench testing is entirely optional
Raise the protected equipment design pressure rating to match the valve
Repair or recondition it and retest before returning it to service
content.explanation: A valve that fails its set-pressure test is repaired/reconditioned and retested to confirm it functions before reinstallation.

content.stem: A common field method for positive material identification under RP 578 is:
options: Handheld X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analysis of the component
Liquid penetrant examination of the bare component outer surface
Magnetic particle examination of the completed welded pipe joint
Radiographic film exposure taken of the full pipe circumference
content.explanation: XRF (and optical emission) analyzers confirm alloy composition in the field; PT/MT/RT are flaw methods, not composition checks.

content.stem: An effective PMI program under RP 578 verifies alloy material primarily at:
options: Only the final exterior painting stage of the overall project
Receipt and installation of alloy components in critical service
The lunch and rest breaks of the receiving inspection crew members
The point in time where the relief valve is bench tested off line
content.explanation: PMI checks alloys at receipt and during installation (and sometimes existing assets) to prevent incorrect-material installation in critical service.

content.stem: The principal risk RP 578 addresses by verifying materials is that:
options: A welder qualification record could quietly expire during the work
An incorrect exterior paint color could be applied to the pipe run
A wrong alloy could fail prematurely in its intended service
A relief valve discharge line could be sized substantially too large
content.explanation: Material mix-ups (e.g., carbon steel where an alloy is required) can fail prematurely; PMI guards against that consequence.

content.stem: ASME B31.3 normal fluid service generally requires what examination of welds?
options: No examination of any kind at all for normal fluid service piping welds
Full volumetric radiography of every single weld without any exception
Visual examination plus a defined percentage of random radiography
Only an exterior protective repaint applied over each completed weld
content.explanation: Normal fluid service requires visual examination of all welds and random RT (a defined percentage), with more for higher categories.

content.stem: ASME B31.3 permits which alternative when a hydrostatic leak test is not practical?
options: An exterior protective repaint of the piping in place of any testing
Skipping any leak verification at all of the completed piping system
An automatic rerate of the whole system to a much lower pressure level
A pneumatic test, or other code-permitted alternative, with added precautions
content.explanation: Where hydro is impractical, B31.3 allows a pneumatic test (with safeguards) or other permitted alternatives such as a sensitive leak test.

content.stem: A sensitive leak test in ASME B31.3 is intended for:
options: Detecting very small leaks where high tightness is needed
Replacing the pressure-design calculation of the pipe
Setting the corrosion allowance for the piping system
Establishing the welder qualification for the project
content.explanation: The sensitive leak test (e.g., per Article 10 methods) finds small leaks where a high degree of tightness is required.

content.stem: The soil-to-air interface on partially buried piping warrants special attention because it:
options: Is always the single thickest section of the entire piping run length
Experiences moisture and aeration changes that accelerate corrosion
Carries no process fluid at all and therefore simply cannot corrode
Only affects the legibility of the line identification tag at grade
content.explanation: The soil-to-air interface sees wet/dry and aeration cycling, making it a classic external-corrosion hot spot on buried piping.

content.stem: Monitoring a cathodic protection system on buried piping primarily confirms that:
options: The relief device set pressure is correct on the unit
The exterior paint color matches the original spec
Protective potentials are being maintained along the line
The pipe nominal schedule number has not changed
content.explanation: CP surveys verify that protective potentials are maintained; loss of protection signals renewed external corrosion risk.

content.stem: When both a short-term and a long-term corrosion rate are available, API 570 practice is to:
options: Use the rate that yields the more conservative remaining life
Always use the long-term rate regardless of recent data
Average the two rates and ignore any recent acceleration
Use whichever rate gives the longest possible interval
content.explanation: The rate giving the more conservative (shorter) remaining life is used, so recent acceleration is not masked by older data.

content.stem: A through-wall leak discovered on an in-service piping system should be:
options: Painted over on the exterior surface to stop the visible dripping
Ignored entirely until the next regularly scheduled turnaround
Offset simply by raising the overall system design pressure rating
Evaluated and repaired or removed from service per the program
content.explanation: A leak is assessed for cause and severity and repaired (temporary then permanent) or the system is shut down, per the integrity program.

content.stem: CMLs on a circuit with expected localized corrosion should be:
options: Spread evenly with no regard to the damage type
Concentrated where the localized loss is most likely
Placed only on the exterior painted surfaces
Limited to a single location per piping circuit
content.explanation: Where damage is localized (injection points, dead legs, turbulence), CMLs are concentrated there rather than spread uniformly.

content.stem: Class 1 piping in API 570 generally receives more frequent inspection because it:
options: Carries the highest potential consequence on a release
Is always the single shortest run within the whole process unit
Has the brightest exterior protective paint color that is applied
Contains the fewest individual welds of any defined piping class
content.explanation: Class 1 covers the highest-consequence services, so it gets the closest inspection attention and shortest intervals.

content.stem: A dissimilar-metal flanged connection in a wet service shows preferential metal loss on the less-noble side. Which mechanism fits?
options: Sour water corrosion (acidic)
Mechanical fatigue cracking
Soil-side external corrosion
Galvanic corrosion
content.explanation: A dissimilar-metal couple in a wet (conductive) joint drives galvanic attack on the less-noble (anodic) metal.

content.stem: A carbon-steel line in low-pH water containing H2S shows general and localized thinning. Which mechanism fits?
options: Sour water corrosion (acidic)
Galvanic corrosion of the couple
Mechanical fatigue cracking
Soil-side external corrosion
content.explanation: Low-pH (acidic) sour water with H2S corrodes carbon steel; rate increases with H2S content, velocity, and falling pH.

content.stem: Straight seamless pipe, OD D = 18.0 in, P = 420 psi, S = 18900 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness from t = PD/(2(SEW + PY))?
options: 0.2 in

content.stem: Straight pipe, OD D = 5.563 in, P = 700 psi, S = 16700 psi, E = 0.85 (ERW), W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. Pressure-design thickness?
An in-service seamless pipe, OD D = 16.0 in, current measured wall t = 0.375 in, S = 20000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0, Y = 0.4. MAWP from P = 2tSEW/(D - 2Yt)?
A pipe's B31.3 pressure-design thickness is 0.205 in and a 0.060 in corrosion allowance is specified. Required minimum thickness (t + c)?
content.explanation: Required minimum thickness = pressure-design thickness + corrosion allowance = 0.205 + 0.060 = 0.265 in.

content.stem: A CML read 0.438 in fifteen years ago and reads 0.288 in today. Long-term corrosion rate?
options: 0.01 in/yr
0.02 in/yr
0.005 in/yr
content.explanation: Long-term rate = (t_initial - t_actual)/time = (0.438 - 0.288)/15 = 0.01 in/yr.

content.stem: t_actual = 0.288 in, t_required = 0.165 in, corrosion rate = 0.011 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 11.2 years
26.2 years
5.6 years
15 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_required)/rate = (0.288 - 0.165)/0.011 = 11.2 years.

content.stem: A piping circuit has a remaining life of 13 years. The class maximum thickness-measurement interval is 5 years. What inspection interval applies?
options: 13 years
6.5 years
5 years
2.5 years
content.explanation: Interval = lesser of half the remaining life (6.5 yr) or the class maximum (5 yr); the class maximum governs at 5 years.

content.stem: Per ASME B31.3, with equal test and design temperatures, the minimum hydrostatic leak-test pressure for a 610 psi design pressure is:
options: 793 psi
915 psi
671 psi
610 psi
content.explanation: Minimum hydrostatic test pressure = 1.5 x design pressure = 1.5 x 610 = 915 psi (equal test and design temperatures).

content.stem: A vertical line has a design pressure of 175 psi at the top. A point is 95 ft below (SG = 1.0). Total pressure at that point?
options: 175 psi
41.1 psi
content.explanation: Total = design pressure + static head = 175 + (0.433 x 95) = 216.1 psi.

content.stem: An effective piping inspection plan is organized primarily around:
options: The credible damage mechanisms and where they are expected to act
A single fixed checklist applied identically to every piping circuit run
The exterior protective paint scheme chosen for the piping system
The total number of pipe supports counted along the pipe rack run
content.explanation: The plan targets the credible mechanisms and their likely locations, selecting methods and CMLs accordingly.

content.stem: Grouping piping into inspection circuits is useful because it lets the inspector:
options: Avoid having to record any thickness data for the grouped lines at all
Manage lines of similar service and corrosion together for monitoring
Permanently raise the design pressure rating of the grouped piping runs
Exempt the grouped lines entirely from the owner-user inspection program
content.explanation: A circuit groups piping with similar metallurgy, service, and expected corrosion so monitoring and rate analysis can be managed coherently.

content.stem: Selecting an NDE method for a suspected cracking mechanism in piping favors:
options: A pressure test alone, with no supporting surface examination at all
Only ultrasonic thickness gauging to track the general wall loss rate
Exterior paint inspection in place of any surface examination method
Surface methods such as PT or MT that reveal surface-breaking cracks
content.explanation: Surface-breaking cracking (e.g., SCC, fatigue) is found with surface methods (PT/MT) or angle-beam UT, not by thickness gauging alone.

content.stem: Instrument and auxiliary small-bore connections are included in the inspection program because they:
options: Can fail from corrosion, fatigue, or mechanical damage despite small size
Always carry the very highest process pressure within the entire unit
Are completely exempt from the owner-user piping inspection program
Only matter for the legibility of the instrument identification tags
content.explanation: Small-bore instrument/auxiliary lines fail more often than their size implies, from vibration, corrosion, and mechanical damage.

content.stem: When new thickness data show a higher corrosion rate than assumed, the inspector should:
options: Repaint the line exterior to slow the internal corrosion that was found
Disregard the new readings until the next scheduled unit turnaround
Raise the system design pressure to offset the additional metal loss
Recompute remaining life and shorten the inspection interval as needed
content.explanation: A higher measured rate shortens remaining life, so the remaining life and interval are recalculated and tightened.

content.stem: A repair organization performing welded repairs on in-service piping must:
options: Work without any written procedure as long as it moves quickly enough
Use qualified procedures and welders under the inspector's oversight
Set its own acceptance criteria independent of the construction code
Be exempt from documentation because the work is only temporary in nature
content.explanation: Repairs use qualified WPS/welders, follow the applicable code, and are documented under inspector oversight.

content.stem: Choosing a representative set of CMLs rather than measuring everywhere is acceptable when the CMLs:
options: Are placed solely on the exterior painted surface of the piping run
Are chosen only at the points that are easiest to physically reach
Capture the locations and types of damage credible for that circuit
Are limited to one single location regardless of the circuit length
content.explanation: Representative CMLs are valid when they cover the credible damage locations/types; convenience-only placement misses real loss.

content.stem: If an inspection interval is extended on a risk basis, the supporting analysis should be:
options: Replaced by simply repainting the exterior of the piping run
Kept only in the inspector's memory without any written record
Documented and retained as part of the integrity program records
Discarded once the extended interval has been put into effect
content.explanation: Risk-based interval extensions are documented and retained so the basis can be reviewed and audited.

content.stem: PCC-2 Article 101 (Introduction) establishes that a selected repair method should be:
options: Selected purely on the color of the exterior protective coating
Chosen only on the basis of the lowest possible material cost
Applied without any evaluation of the underlying defect at all
Suitable for the damage, the service, and the remaining design life
content.explanation: Article 101 frames repair selection around suitability for the damage, service conditions, loads, and remaining life.

content.stem: Using NDE in lieu of a pressure test (Article 502) is appropriate mainly when:
options: A pressure test is impractical and qualified NDE can verify the repair
The repair organization simply prefers to skip the leak verification
The system design pressure is being raised without any basis at all
The exterior of the repaired piping has just been freshly repainted
content.explanation: Article 502 substitutes qualified NDE for a pressure test where testing is impractical, with the examination demonstrating integrity.

content.stem: Pressure design of a closure (such as a cap or blind end) in B31.3 is handled by:
options: Ignoring pressure design because closures never see internal pressure
Applying the listed-component rating or the applicable design rules
Using only the exterior paint thickness as the design parameter
Counting the flange bolts and applying no other consideration at all
content.explanation: Closures are designed by listed-component ratings or the applicable B31.3 rules for the geometry, not left unanalyzed.

content.stem: The pressure-design thickness of a reducer in B31.3 is determined by:
options: Counting the number of welds at each end of the reducer fitting
Assuming it is always thinner than the smaller connected pipe end
Using the exterior coating thickness over the reducer body only
Applying the pressure-design rules using the controlling diameter
content.explanation: Reducer pressure design follows the B31.3 component rules referencing 304.1 with the governing diameter.

content.stem: ASME B31.3 imposes more stringent examination on severe cyclic and high-pressure service because:
options: Those services carry higher consequence and damage potential
Those services always use a brighter exterior paint color
Those services contain fewer welds than normal fluid service
Those services are exempt from any visual examination at all
content.explanation: Higher-category services (severe cyclic, high pressure) get more examination because failure consequence and damage potential are greater.

content.stem: Hardness testing after PWHT on certain steels is performed to confirm that:
options: The relief valve set pressure on the line is still correct
The exterior paint adhered properly over the heat-treated weld
The heat treatment achieved acceptable hardness in the weld zone
The pipe nominal schedule number has not changed at all
content.explanation: Post-PWHT hardness checks confirm the treatment reduced weld/HAZ hardness to acceptable levels for the service.

content.stem: RP 574 indicates the number of TMLs on a circuit should increase when the circuit has:
options: A lower process temperature than the rest of the unit
A brighter exterior paint color than the adjacent circuits
Fewer fittings and a longer uninterrupted straight run
Higher corrosion rates or a higher consequence of failure
content.explanation: More TMLs are warranted where corrosion is higher or consequence is greater, to characterize the condition adequately.

content.stem: A rupture disk used as overpressure protection differs from a relief valve in that it:
options: Opens by bursting and does not reclose after relieving
Always reseats automatically after the overpressure ends
Requires no inspection because it has no moving parts
Sets the protected equipment design pressure by itself
content.explanation: A rupture disk is non-reclosing; once burst it must be replaced, and it is inspected for corrosion, fatigue, and correct installation.

content.stem: RP 577 notes that postweld heat treatment is used chiefly to:
options: Improve the exterior paint adhesion over the weld
Relieve residual stress and reduce weld-zone hardness
Shorten the welder performance qualification test
Increase the corrosion allowance of the base metal
content.explanation: PWHT relieves residual stresses and tempers the weld/HAZ, lowering hardness and cracking susceptibility in susceptible steels.

content.stem: RP 578 records of a positive material identification should capture, for traceability:
options: Just the operator rest-break times during the alloy testing
Only the exterior paint batch and the topcoat color code
The component, the method used, and the verified alloy result
Only the relief valve set pressure on the connected circuit
content.explanation: PMI records document what was tested, the method, and the confirmed alloy, supporting traceability and audit.

content.stem: The base-metal thickness range a procedure qualifies is governed in Section IX by:
options: The exterior protective coating applied after the welding
The thickness of the test coupon and the QW-451 range rules
The number of flanges installed on the finished piping run
The brand of the welding power supply used during the test
content.explanation: Qualified base-metal thickness range derives from the coupon thickness per the QW-451 tables.

content.stem: The Procedure Qualification Record (PQR) in Section IX documents:
options: Just the welder's personal break schedule during the test weld
Only the exterior coatings applied after the welding is complete
The actual values used and the test results that support a WPS
Only the relief valve set-pressure history of the connected line
content.explanation: The PQR records the as-welded variables and mechanical-test results that qualify and support the WPS.

content.stem: The gasket selected for a B16.5 flanged joint must be compatible with the:
options: Relief valve set pressure on a separate process circuit
Exterior protective paint color of the connected run
Welder qualification used elsewhere on the piping unit
Flange facing, the service fluid, and the temperature
content.explanation: Gasket choice depends on the facing type, the fluid/service, the temperature, and the required seating; it must suit all of these.

content.stem: The allowable working pressure of a B16.5 flange at a given temperature is found from:
options: The pressure-temperature rating table for its class and material group
The exterior paint thickness that was applied to the flange body
The number of bolt holes that are present in the flange ring
The length of the pipe run that is attached to the flange face
content.explanation: B16.5 rating tables give allowable pressure by class and material group as a function of temperature.

content.stem: A small-bore vent line off a vibrating compressor discharge cracks at the branch weld after a period of service. Which mechanism fits?
options: Soil-side external corrosion
Mechanical fatigue (vibration-induced)
Galvanic corrosion of the couple
Sour water corrosion (acidic)
content.explanation: Cyclic vibration concentrating at the small-bore branch weld drives vibration-induced mechanical fatigue cracking.

content.stem: A stagnant, water-holding low-point drain develops under-deposit pitting with biological fouling. Which mechanism fits?
options: Galvanic corrosion of the couple
Mechanical fatigue cracking
Microbiologically influenced corrosion
Soil-side external corrosion
content.explanation: Stagnant, water-wetted, deposit-laden low points with biofilms point to MIC as localized under-deposit pitting.

content.stem: Tank diameter D = 120 ft, fill height H = 40 ft, product specific gravity G = 1.0, allowable stress S = 23200 psi, joint efficiency E = 0.85. API 653 minimum shell thickness from t = 2.6 D (H-1) G/(S E)?
content.explanation: t = (2.6 x 120 x (40-1) x 1.0)/(23200 x 0.85) = 0.617 in. The (H-1) places the design point one foot above the bottom of the course.

content.stem: Tank diameter D = 100 ft, fill height H = 48 ft, G = 0.95, S = 26000 psi, E = 1.0 (fully radiographed). API 653 minimum shell thickness?
Same tank (D = 120 ft, H = 40 ft, G = 1.0, S = 23200 psi) but the seam is not radiographed, so E = 0.70. API 653 minimum shell thickness?
content.explanation: t = (2.6 x 120 x 39 x 1.0)/(23200 x 0.70) = 0.7493 in. A lower joint efficiency raises the required thickness for the same service.

content.stem: Tank D = 90 ft, H = 36 ft, product G = 1.1, S = 25000 psi, E = 0.85. API 653 minimum shell thickness?
content.explanation: t = (2.6 x 90 x (36-1) x 1.1)/(25000 x 0.85) = 0.424 in. A denser product (higher G) raises the hydrostatic load and the required thickness.

content.stem: A shell course has an available thickness of 0.50 in for pressure design. With D = 120 ft, G = 1.0, S = 23200 psi, E = 0.85, the maximum fill height from H = tSE/(2.6 D G) + 1 is:
content.explanation: H = (0.50 x 23200 x 0.85)/(2.6 x 120 x 1.0) + 1 = 32.6 ft. The +1 inverts the (H-1) design-point offset.

content.stem: A shell course measured 0.500 in eight years ago and 0.436 in today. Corrosion rate?
options: 0.016 in/yr
0.004 in/yr
0.008 in/yr
content.explanation: Rate = (t_previous - t_actual)/time = (0.500 - 0.436)/8 = 0.008 in/yr.

content.stem: Shell course: t_actual = 0.436 in, t_min = 0.300 in, corrosion rate = 0.008 in/yr. Remaining life?
options: 37.5 years
54.5 years
8.5 years
17 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - t_min)/rate = (0.436 - 0.300)/0.008 = 17 years.

content.stem: A tank bottom has a remaining corrosion allowance of 0.150 in and a measured bottom corrosion rate of 0.012 in/yr. The computed internal-inspection interval (before applying the 20-year cap) is:
options: 25 years
12.5 years
20.8 years
6.2 years
content.explanation: Interval = remaining corrosion allowance / corrosion rate = 0.150/0.012 = 12.5 years, which is below the 20-year ceiling, so it governs.

content.stem: A tank bottom has a remaining corrosion allowance of 0.180 in and a measured corrosion rate of 0.006 in/yr. What internal-inspection interval applies?
options: 15 years
30 years
20 years
10 years
content.explanation: Computed interval = 0.180/0.006 = 30 years, but API 653 caps the internal interval at 20 years absent an RBI assessment, so 20 years applies.

content.stem: Concentration cell corrosion on a tank bottom is driven by:
options: A single applied tensile stress with no chemistry or deposit involved
A uniform high temperature applied evenly across the entire tank floor
The exterior paint color selected for the tank shell courses above
Local differences in oxygen or ion concentration across the metal surface
content.explanation: Concentration cells form where deposits, crevices, or gaskets create differential oxygen/ion concentrations, producing localized anodic attack.

content.stem: A tank floor develops pitting beneath sludge and debris deposits, worst at the deposit edges. Which mechanism best fits?
options: Concentration cell corrosion
Brittle fracture of the floor plate
Caustic stress corrosion cracking
Sulfuric acid corrosion at velocity
content.explanation: Differential aeration under deposits sets up a concentration cell; the oxygen-starved area under the deposit becomes anodic and pits.

content.stem: Ethanol stress corrosion cracking of carbon steel is a concern primarily in:
options: Dry nitrogen blanketing gas with no ethanol present at all in service
Fuel-grade ethanol service, especially at welds and stressed regions
The exterior protective coating applied over the tank shell plates
High-temperature steam service well above the creep threshold range
content.explanation: Ethanol SCC affects carbon steel in fuel-grade ethanol, concentrating at welds and high-stress areas; oxygen and galvanic effects aggravate it.

content.stem: A carbon-steel tank storing fuel-grade ethanol develops cracks at non-stress-relieved weld seams. Which mechanism best fits?
options: Soil-side corrosion of the floor
Concentration cell corrosion
Ethanol stress corrosion cracking
Atmospheric corrosion of the shell
content.explanation: Cracking at welds in fuel-grade ethanol service points to ethanol SCC, driven by residual weld stress and the ethanol environment.

content.stem: Sulfuric acid corrosion of carbon steel is strongly influenced by:
options: The welder qualification record for the bottom annular ring
The exterior paint gloss measured on the tank shell course
Acid concentration and flow velocity at the metal surface
The number of roof support columns inside the storage tank
content.explanation: Sulfuric acid attack on steel depends on concentration and velocity; protective iron-sulfate films are stripped at higher velocities, accelerating loss.

content.stem: Microbiologically influenced corrosion on a tank bottom is most associated with:
options: A uniformly high process temperature across the whole tank floor
Dry, well-drained sand with no water present beneath the floor
The exterior shell paint system applied above the chime angle
Stagnant water bottoms, deposits, and biofilm under the sediment
content.explanation: MIC thrives in stagnant water bottoms with deposits and biofilms, producing localized under-deposit pitting on the floor.

content.stem: Soil-side corrosion of a tank bottom is governed largely by:
options: Soil resistivity, moisture, and aeration beneath the tank floor
The interior product specific gravity stored within the tank
The exterior shell paint color selected for the tank courses
The number of nozzles installed in the fixed roof structure
content.explanation: Soil-side floor corrosion depends on soil resistivity, moisture, and oxygen access; it is mitigated by cathodic protection and under-tank liners.

content.stem: A tank floor shows external (soil-side) general and pitting loss correlating with low soil resistivity and poor drainage. Which mechanism best fits?
options: Caustic corrosion of the shell
Soil corrosion
Concentration cell at a gasket
Brittle fracture of the plate
content.explanation: Soil-side floor loss tied to low resistivity and moisture is classic soil corrosion, addressed by cathodic protection and proper pads.

content.stem: API 653 distinguishes the external inspection from the internal inspection mainly because:
options: The internal inspection covers only the exterior shell paint condition
The external inspection can only be performed by the operating company alone
The internal inspection requires the tank to be out of service and cleaned
The external inspection requires a full hydrostatic test on every occasion
content.explanation: The internal (out-of-service) inspection accesses the floor and lower internals; the external inspection is done in service on a different interval.

content.stem: The API 653 external inspection interval generally has a not-to-exceed limit of:
options: Twenty years regardless of the measured shell corrosion rate at all
Five years, or a shorter interval based on the shell corrosion rate
Two years for every tank irrespective of its service or condition
Whatever interval the operating crew finds convenient to schedule
content.explanation: External inspections are performed at intervals not exceeding 5 years (shorter if the corrosion rate or condition warrants).

content.stem: The API 653 internal inspection interval is governed primarily by:
options: The brand of the welding electrodes used on the original bottom
The exterior shell paint condition observed during a routine round
The number of shell courses welded into the tank during erection
The tank bottom corrosion rate and remaining corrosion allowance
content.explanation: The internal interval is set from the bottom-plate minimum thickness, remaining allowance, and corrosion rate, capped (often 20 years) absent RBI.

content.stem: Under API 653, an alteration differs from a repair in that an alteration:
options: Only repaints the exterior shell without touching any structural plate
Changes the tank physically beyond restoring it to a condition for service
Is always smaller in scope than the simplest weld-overlay repair job
Never requires any engineering evaluation before the work proceeds
content.explanation: A repair restores integrity to a suitable-for-service condition; an alteration changes the tank (e.g., height, nozzles) beyond simple restoration.

content.stem: Reconstruction under API 653 refers to work where a tank is:
options: Dismantled and reassembled, often relocated, to return it to service
Simply repainted in place with no plate work performed at all
Inspected externally without ever being taken out of service
Fitted with a new gauge while remaining completely in operation
content.explanation: Reconstruction covers dismantling and reassembly (often at a new site), with specific API 653 requirements for the rebuilt tank.

content.stem: API 653 brittle-fracture assessment of an existing tank gives weight to:
options: Material toughness, thickness, and the minimum metal temperature in service
The exterior shell paint color and its measured surface gloss level
The number of stairway treads installed on the external platform
The brand of level gauge fitted to the fixed roof of the tank
content.explanation: Brittle-fracture screening considers toughness, thickness, stress, and the lowest expected metal temperature, often via an evaluation procedure.

content.stem: When measured shell thickness falls below the minimum required, API 653 calls for:
options: Ignoring the reading until the next scheduled external inspection
Immediate repainting of the exterior shell to restore the thickness
An evaluation that may require repair, rerating, or removal from service
Raising the product specific gravity to compensate for the thinning
content.explanation: Below-minimum thickness triggers a suitability evaluation; outcomes include repair, fill-height reduction (rerate), or taking the tank out of service.

content.stem: The annular plate ring in an API 650 tank is provided primarily to:
options: Serve as the exterior walking platform around the tank base
Carry the higher stresses at the shell-to-bottom junction region
Act as the sole roof support column inside the storage tank
Provide the gauge connection for measuring the product level
content.explanation: Annular plates handle the elevated shell-to-bottom junction stresses and are thicker than the interior bottom plates.

content.stem: The joint efficiency used in the API 653 shell-thickness formula depends on:
options: The extent of radiographic examination of the shell weld seams
The exterior paint thickness applied over the finished shell weld
The number of courses stacked to build up the tank shell height
The color coding applied to the tank nozzle identification tags
content.explanation: Joint efficiency reflects the degree of weld examination (e.g., spot vs full RT), so more radiography supports a higher E.

content.stem: An internal floating roof is used in a fixed-roof tank mainly to:
options: Serve as the primary cathodic protection anode for the floor
Increase the hydrostatic head applied to the bottom plates
Reduce vapor space and evaporative loss of the stored product
Provide the exterior coating system for the tank shell courses
content.explanation: An internal floating roof floats on the liquid to minimize the vapor space and evaporative/emission losses.

content.stem: A wind girder on an open-top tank is provided to:
options: Provide the electrical ground connection for the tank shell
Store the product overflow during a high-fill upset event
Act as the main walkway support for the external stairway
Maintain the roundness of the shell against wind loading
content.explanation: Wind girders (stiffening rings) preserve shell roundness and stability against wind on open-top tanks.

content.stem: RP 575 identifies which method as well suited to screening a tank floor for underside corrosion?
options: Magnetic flux leakage (MFL) scanning of the floor plates
Exterior shell paint gloss measurement around the chime
Counting the number of roof vents on the fixed roof
Reviewing the welder qualification paperwork for the seams
content.explanation: MFL floor scanning rapidly screens bottom plates for top- and underside metal loss, with UT follow-up on indications.

content.stem: RP 575 notes a vacuum box is used on a tank bottom to:
options: Measure the remaining thickness of the annular plate ring
Detect through-leaks in the floor weld seams with a soap solution
Apply the cathodic protection potential to the floor plates
Establish the joint efficiency value for the shell courses
content.explanation: A vacuum box over a soaped weld reveals through-leaks by drawing bubbles, used to test bottom and patch welds for tightness.

content.stem: RP 575 inspection of tank foundation settlement is important because excessive settlement can:
options: Increase the allowable fill height of the tank automatically
Improve the exterior paint adhesion on the lower shell course
Overstress the shell and bottom and impair floating-roof operation
Eliminate the need for any cathodic protection of the floor
content.explanation: Differential/edge settlement can overstress the shell-to-bottom region and bind a floating roof, so it is monitored and evaluated.

content.stem: RP 575 attributes water bottoms in a storage tank to a heightened risk of:
options: Overpressure of the fixed roof from thermal vapor expansion
Brittle fracture of the upper shell course in warm weather
Loss of the exterior shell paint above the liquid level line
Internal bottom corrosion and microbial activity at the floor
content.explanation: Settled water bottoms promote floor corrosion and MIC, so water draw-off and housekeeping are emphasized.

content.stem: RP 651 cathodic protection of a tank bottom protects against corrosion on the:
options: Soil-side (external underside) surface of the bottom plates
Interior fixed-roof rafters above the stored product level
Exterior shell paint surface above the tank chime angle
Gauge float mechanism mounted on the fixed roof nozzle
content.explanation: CP mitigates soil-side (underside) bottom corrosion by making the floor cathodic relative to the soil environment.

content.stem: An impressed-current cathodic protection system differs from a sacrificial-anode system in that it:
options: Requires no monitoring once it is installed beneath the tank
Uses an external power source to drive protective current to the floor
Protects only the exterior shell paint rather than the floor
Always uses magnesium anodes connected directly to the shell
content.explanation: Impressed current uses a rectifier/power source and inert anodes; sacrificial systems rely on galvanic anodes (e.g., magnesium) without external power.

content.stem: RP 651 confirms adequate cathodic protection of a tank bottom by:
options: Counting the number of anodes visible around the tank perimeter
Checking the exterior shell paint thickness over the chime angle
Measuring structure-to-soil potentials against an accepted criterion
Verifying the welder qualification used on the bottom seams
content.explanation: CP adequacy is judged by structure-to-soil potential measurements meeting an accepted criterion (e.g., a polarized potential basis).

content.stem: An internal tank-bottom lining under RP 652 is applied primarily to:
options: Provide the exterior cathodic protection anode bed for the floor
Increase the joint efficiency of the shell weld seams above
Serve as the wind girder for an open-top storage tank
Isolate the floor from the product to prevent internal bottom corrosion
content.explanation: Internal linings form a barrier between the stored product/water and the steel floor, preventing product-side bottom corrosion.

content.stem: RP 652 stresses surface preparation before lining application because:
options: Lining adhesion and performance depend on a properly prepared substrate
It sets the joint efficiency value used in the shell calculation
It establishes the cathodic protection potential of the floor
It determines the maximum fill height permitted for the tank
content.explanation: Proper cleaning and profile (e.g., abrasive blasting) are essential for lining adhesion and service life; poor prep leads to early failure.

content.stem: After a tank-bottom lining is installed, RP 652 calls for checking it for:
options: The exterior shell paint color match to the adjacent tanks
Holidays, thickness, and adhesion before returning the tank to service
The number of roof vents fitted to the fixed roof structure
The welder qualification used on the original shell courses
content.explanation: Lining QC includes holiday (pinhole) detection, dry-film thickness, and adhesion checks before service.

content.stem: API 653 bottom evaluation uses MRT = min(RTbc, RTip) - Or(StPr + UPr). With RTbc = 0.180 in (underside), RTip = 0.200 in (topside), Or = 10 yr, StPr = 0.004 in/yr, UPr = 0.003 in/yr, the MRT at the next inspection is:
content.explanation: min(RTbc, RTip) = 0.180. MRT = 0.180 - 10 x (0.004 + 0.003) = 0.11 in. Both topside and underside rates are deducted over the interval.

content.stem: Using MRT = min(RTbc, RTip) - Or(StPr + UPr): the topside is coated with a coating life exceeding Or, so StPr = 0. With RTbc = 0.150 in, RTip = 0.220 in, Or = 8 yr, UPr = 0.005 in/yr, the MRT is:
content.explanation: Coated topside meeting the coating-life rule gives StPr = 0. min(RTbc, RTip) = 0.150, so MRT = 0.150 - 8 x (0 + 0.005) = 0.11 in.

content.stem: Rearranging the MRT relation, the maximum in-service interval is Or = (min(RTbc, RTip) - MRT)/(StPr + UPr). With min(RTbc, RTip) = 0.250 in, a required MRT = 0.100 in, StPr = 0.006 in/yr, UPr = 0.004 in/yr, Or is:
options: 25 years
15 years
37.5 years
10 years
content.explanation: Or = (0.250 - 0.100)/(0.006 + 0.004) = 0.150/0.010 = 15 years, then capped at the 6.4.2 internal ceiling if lower.

content.stem: API 653 sets the critical-zone minimum bottom thickness as the smaller of (1/2 the original bottom thickness) or (50% of the lower-shell-course tmin), but not less than 0.1 in. Original bottom = 0.25 in, lower-shell tmin = 0.30 in. The critical-zone minimum is:
options: 0.1 in
content.explanation: 0.5 x 0.25 = 0.125; 0.5 x 0.30 = 0.150; the smaller is 0.125 in, which exceeds the 0.1 in floor, so 0.125 in governs. This minimum applies within the critical zone - the annular band within 3 in. of the shell (3.10).

content.stem: Using the same rule (smaller of 1/2 original bottom or 50% of lower-shell tmin, not less than 0.1 in): original bottom = 0.18 in, lower-shell tmin = 0.16 in. The critical-zone minimum is:
options: 0.1 in
content.explanation: 0.5 x 0.18 = 0.09 and 0.5 x 0.16 = 0.08; the smaller is 0.08, but the rule sets a 0.1 in floor, so 0.1 in governs. This minimum applies within the critical zone - the annular band within 3 in. of the shell (3.10).

content.stem: A tank bottom has a minimum measured thickness of 0.230 in, a required MRT of 0.100 in, and a combined (topside + underside) corrosion rate of 0.0065 in/yr. Remaining life of the bottom?
options: 15.4 years
35.4 years
10 years
20 years
content.explanation: Remaining life = (t_actual - MRT)/combined rate = (0.230 - 0.100)/0.0065 = 20 years.

content.stem: On a multi-course tank (D = 120 ft), an upper course has H = 16 ft measured from the bottom of that course to the maximum liquid level. With G = 1.0, S = 26000 psi, E = 0.85, the API 653 minimum thickness for that course is:
content.explanation: t = (2.6 x 120 x (16-1) x 1.0)/(26000 x 0.85) = 0.2118 in. H is taken from the bottom of the course being evaluated.

content.stem: A bottom shell course has 0.62 in available for pressure design. With D = 100 ft, G = 0.95, S = 24000 psi, E = 1.0, the maximum fill height from H = tSE/(2.6 D G) + 1 is:
content.explanation: H = (0.62 x 24000 x 1.0)/(2.6 x 100 x 0.95) + 1 = 61.24 ft. The +1 inverts the (H-1) design-point offset.

content.stem: API 653 permits a lower minimum bottom-plate thickness (such as 0.05 in) when the tank has:
options: A means to provide both detection and containment of a bottom leak
A brighter exterior shell paint color than the surrounding tanks
A larger number of roof support columns inside the storage tank
A higher product specific gravity than originally designed for
content.explanation: Table 4.4 allows a thinner bottom minimum (e.g., 0.05 in) where a release prevention barrier with leak detection/containment exists; otherwise the minimum is higher.

content.stem: The critical zone of a tank bottom that API 653 treats with stricter thickness limits is the:
options: Exact geometric center point of the tank bottom plates
Annular region of the bottom near the shell-to-bottom joint
Exterior chime edge that projects beyond the shell wall
Topmost shell course furthest from the tank bottom plates
content.explanation: The critical zone is the bottom annulus near the shell-to-bottom junction, where stresses are highest and the stricter minimum applies.

content.stem: API 653 treats isolated pitting on a tank bottom as:
options: A reason to raise the maximum fill height of the storage tank
Always requiring immediate full replacement of the entire bottom
Not appreciably affecting plate strength if within defined limits
Irrelevant to leak potential regardless of the pit depth at all
content.explanation: Scattered isolated pits do not appreciably reduce plate strength within limits, but through-wall pitting is a leak concern and is evaluated separately.

content.stem: In the API 653 bottom MRT relation, RTbc and RTip represent, respectively, the remaining thickness after repairs from:
options: The nozzle neck thinning and the flange face corrosion damage
The shell course corrosion and the fixed-roof plate corrosion
The exterior paint loss and the interior lining degradation rate
Underside (soil-side) corrosion and topside (internal) corrosion
content.explanation: RTbc is the minimum remaining thickness from bottom-side (underside) loss and RTip from topside (internal) loss, both after any repairs.

content.stem: Setting StPr = 0 in the bottom MRT calculation is permitted when:
options: The topside is coated and the coating life equals or exceeds the interval
The tank has any exterior protective shell paint applied above the chime angle
The product specific gravity is below one for the particular stored fluid
The tank has more than a set number of fixed-roof vents fitted to it
content.explanation: StPr (topside corrosion rate) may be taken as zero for coated areas only if the coating's expected life meets or exceeds the in-service interval Or.

content.stem: Magnetic flux leakage (MFL) floor scanning is typically paired with which follow-up method?
options: Reviewing the welder qualification records for the bottom seams
Exterior shell paint gloss measurement around the tank chime
Counting the number of fixed-roof vents on the tank roof
Ultrasonic thickness measurement to quantify the indicated loss
content.explanation: MFL rapidly locates floor metal loss; UT then quantifies the remaining thickness at the flagged indications.

content.stem: Uniform (planar) settlement of a tank, where the whole tank moves down evenly, is generally:
options: The most damaging type, always cracking the shell-to-bottom weld
The least damaging type, though it can still strain connected piping
A reason to immediately increase the tank's maximum fill height
Impossible to occur on any properly founded storage tank at all
content.explanation: Uniform settlement is the least harmful to the tank itself; its main effect is on connected piping and nozzles, which may need releveling.

content.stem: Rigid-body (planar) tilt of a tank is a concern because it:
options: Eliminates the need to evaluate any shell-to-bottom stress
Reduces the hydrostatic load on every shell course equally
Adds liquid head on the low side and can affect a floating roof
Improves the exterior paint adhesion on the low-side shell
content.explanation: A rigid tilt raises the effective head on the low side and can bind a floating roof; it is evaluated for its added stress.

content.stem: API 653 evaluates out-of-plane (differential) shell settlement by:
options: Measuring only the single highest survey point recorded on the tank shell
Averaging the exterior shell paint thickness measured around the circumference
Counting the number of nozzles installed on the lowest shell course of the tank
Fitting the measured points to a smooth cosine curve and assessing deviations
content.explanation: Out-of-plane settlement is the deviation of measured elevations from a best-fit cosine curve; the deviations are compared against an allowable.

content.stem: Edge settlement (localized bottom sinking near the shell) is a concern primarily because it:
options: Strains the shell-to-bottom weld and can crack the bottom plates
Increases the joint efficiency of the lower shell course welds
Raises the brittle-fracture exemption temperature of the shell
Lowers the product specific gravity acting on the bottom plates
content.explanation: Edge settlement concentrates strain at the shell-to-bottom junction and bottom, risking cracking, and is evaluated against Annex B limits.

content.stem: Bottom dishing (center settlement of the floor) is evaluated mainly for its effect on:
options: The exterior shell paint color match to nearby tanks
Bottom plate stress and the integrity of the bottom welds
The number of vents required on the fixed tank roof
The welder qualification used on the upper shell course
content.explanation: Dishing (bowl-shaped center settlement) strains the bottom plates and welds, and can pull on the shell-to-bottom connection.

content.stem: A tank settlement survey is performed by measuring:
